* And Ibn Waki' and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Ali ibn Husayn, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: While the Prophet ﷺ was among a group of the Ansar, a star was thrown and it shone brightly. The Prophet ﷺ said: "What did you used to say for such a thing in the Jahiliyyah when you saw it?" They said: "We used to say: a great person dies or a great person is born." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "It is not thrown for the death of anyone or for his life, but our Lord, blessed is His name, when He decrees a matter, the bearers of the Throne glorify, then the people of the heaven who are next to them glorify, then those next to them, until the glorification reaches the people of this heaven. Then the people of the seventh heaven ask the bearers of the Throne: 'What did our Lord say?' and they inform them. Then the people of each heaven inquire until the news reaches the people of the nearest heaven. The devils snatch the hearing and are struck, and they throw what they heard to their allies. What they bring as it was is true, but they add to it."
* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Ibn Shihab narrated to us, from Ali ibn Husayn, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was sitting among a group of his Companions. He said: a star was thrown, and then he mentioned something similar, except that he added in it. I said to al-Zuhri: "Was it thrown in the Jahiliyyah?" He said: "Yes, but it became intensified when the Prophet ﷺ was sent."
* Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Asim ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: My father Ali ibn Asim narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The jinn had seats in the heaven where they heard the revelation. When the revelation was sent down, the angels heard it like the sound of an iron rod struck upon a smooth rock. When the angels heard the sound of the revelation, those in the heaven among the angels fell prostrate on their foreheads. When the people of the revelation came down to them, [the angels] said: '﴿What has your Lord said?﴾ They say: ﴿The truth, and He is the Most High, the Great﴾.' He said: They call out to one another: 'Your Lord is the Truth, and He is the Most High, the Great.' He said: When it came down to the nearest heaven, they said: 'There will be on the earth such and such death, such and such life, such and such drought, such and such abundance, and what He wishes to do and what He wishes to begin, blessed and exalted is He.' Then the jinn descended and conveyed to their allies among mankind what would happen on earth. While they were in that state, God sent the Prophet ﷺ, and the devils were prevented from the heaven and were pelted with stars. No one ascended among them except that he was burned. The people of the earth were alarmed by what they saw in the stars, which had not happened before, and they said: 'Whoever is in the heaven has perished.' The people of al-Ta'if were the first to be alarmed. A man would go to his camels and slaughter a camel every day for their deities, and the owner of sheep would go and slaughter a sheep every day, and the owner of cattle would slaughter a cow every day. A man said to them: 'Woe to you! Do not ruin your wealth, for your landmarks, the stars by which you are guided, have not fallen from them at all.' So they stopped, though they had already hastened to waste their wealth. Iblis said: 'An event has occurred on the earth.' So he was brought soil from every land, and he kept smelling the soil of every land. When he was brought the soil of Tihamah, he said: 'Here the event has occurred.' God turned toward him a group of jinn while he was reciting the Qur'an, and they said: ﴿Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an﴾, until he finished the verse ... and they returned to their people as warners."
* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah informed me, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Urwah, from A'ishah, that she said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: "The angels descend into the clouds, and they mention what has been decreed in the heaven, and the devils steal the hearing, and they hear it and reveal it to the soothsayers, and they lie with it a hundred lies of their own."

These reports indicate that the devils do hear, but they are pelted with shooting stars so that they do not hear.

If someone thinks that, since the word "ila" is in the statement, "seeking to hear" is more fitting for the wording than "hearing," the matter is contrary to what he supposes. The Arabs say: "I heard so-and-so say such and such," "I heard to so-and-so say such and such," and "I heard from so-and-so."

The meaning of the statement is: "We have decorated the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars, and as protection from every rebellious devil, that he not hear the exalted assembly." The word "an" has been omitted, because the context indicates it, as is said: ﴿Thus We have caused it to enter into the hearts of the criminals. They will not believe in it﴾, meaning: that they not believe in it. Had "an" been used in place of "la," it would have been eloquent, as is said: ﴿God makes clear to you lest you go astray﴾, meaning: that you not go astray; and as He said: ﴿And He cast into the earth firm mountains lest it shake with you﴾, meaning: that it not shake with you. The Arabs may use the jussive with "la" in this kind of context, as they say: "I tied the horse so it does not escape," as one of the Banu 'Uqayl said:

*And until we saw the best of affection between us, a cohabitation in which no one who commits evil commits it.*

[The verse is among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (the University photocopy, p. 271), where he said, explaining the verse "they cannot listen": Abd Allah recited it with the doubled sin, meaning "they do not seek to listen," and Ibn 'Abbas also recited it so, and said: "They listen and do not seek to listen." Al-Farra' said: The meaning of "la" is like His words "Thus We have caused it to enter into the hearts of the criminals. They will not believe in it." If "an" could be placed in the place of "la," it would be fitting, as He said: "God makes clear to you lest you go astray," and as He said: "And He cast into the earth firm mountains lest it shake with you." With "la" in this sense, the jussive is also appropriate. The Arabs say: "I tied the horse so it does not escape," and "I bound my slave so he does not run." One of the Banu 'Uqayl recited: "And until we saw ... the verse," and some say: "la yaqrifu al-shar" with the verb in the nominative, and he said: The nominative is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, and the Qur'an came in that.]

It is also reported: "la yaqrifu" with the nominative, and the nominative is said to be the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. Qatadah said regarding this:

* Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾: he said: "They were prevented from it." By His words "to the assembly," he means: to the company of the angels who are higher than those beneath them.
* *
And His words ﴿and are pelted from every side﴾, and they are struck from every direction, meaning: they are struck from every direction of the heaven.

﴿Repelled﴾: the word "duhur" is a verbal noun from your saying: "I repelled him, I repel him, a repulsing and a repelling." The "dahr" is pushing and driving away, and it is said of it: "Repel the devil from yourself," meaning: push him away from you and drive him off.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.
Those who said that:
* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and are pelted from every side, repelled﴾: pelted with shooting stars.
* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and are pelted﴾, "they are struck," ﴿from every side﴾, he said: "from every place."
* *
And His words ﴿repelled﴾

He said: "Driven away."
⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿And they are pelted from every side, repelled﴾: "The devils are repelled by them from listening." And he recited: ﴿Except one who snatches a fleeting word, so there follows him a piercing flame﴾.
* *
And His words ﴿And for them is a perpetual punishment﴾.
Its meaning: "And for these devils who eavesdrop there is a punishment from God, perpetual."
The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of wāṣib (perpetual). Some of them said: its meaning is "painful."
Those who said that:
⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, concerning ﴿And for them is a perpetual punishment﴾: "Painful."
⁕ And Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words ﴿a perpetual punishment﴾: "Painful."
Others said: rather, its meaning is "lasting."
Those who said that:
⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And for them is a perpetual punishment﴾: i.e., lasting.
⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿a perpetual punishment﴾: "Lasting."
⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿And for them is a perpetual punishment﴾: he said, "For them is a lasting punishment."
⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, from one whom he mentioned, from 'Ikrimah, concerning ﴿And for them is a perpetual punishment﴾: "Lasting."
⁕ Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿And for them is a perpetual punishment﴾: "Wāṣib: al-dā'ib (the persistent one)."
The most correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of the one who said: its meaning is "lasting, sincere." This is because God said ﴿And for Him is the religion, perpetual﴾ [Q. 16:52], and it is known that He did not describe it as causing pain and suffering, but rather described it as constancy and sincerity. From this is the verse of Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali:
I do not buy a little praise whose endurance ... is wholly a blame of time, perpetual [[The verse is among the evidences of Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (the Jami'ah photocopy, folio p. 208 – 1), where he said, in explaining the words of the Exalted "a perpetual punishment": lasting. Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali said: "I do not buy the praise..." the verse. End. And in Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' (the Jami'ah photocopy, p. 271): His words "a perpetual punishment" and "And for Him is the religion, perpetual": lasting, sincere. End.]]
i.e., perpetually.
* *
And His words ﴿Except one who snatches the snatching﴾.
He says: "Except one of them who snatches a hearing ﴿so there follows him a piercing flame﴾" meaning: a shining, blazing one.
The interpreters have spoken in accordance with what we have said concerning this.
Those who said that:
⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿so there follows him a piercing flame﴾: from fire; and its piercing is its brightness.
⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words ﴿a piercing flame﴾: he said, "A shining flame which burns him when it is hurled at him."
⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿so there follows him a flame﴾: he said: Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "They are not killed by the flame, nor do they die, but it burns them without killing them, and it makes them mad (yukhabbil) and causes them to miscarry (yukhdij) without killing."
⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿so there follows him a piercing flame﴾: "The piercing one is the one that kindles (al-mustawqid)." He said: "And a man says: 'Athqib nārak' (ignite your fire), and says: 'Istathqib nārak' — kindle your fire."
⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, saying: al-Dahhak was asked, "Do the devils have wings?" He said: "How could they fly to the sky unless they had wings?"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verses 11–12:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So ask them: are they a greater creation, or those whom We have created? Indeed, We created them from clay, sticky clay﴾ (11) ﴿Rather, you wonder, and they mock﴾ (12).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): So ask them, O Muhammad, these polytheists who deny resurrection after death and rising after decay. He says: Ask them, "Are they a greater creation?" That is, is their creation stronger, or the creation of those whom We have created, namely the angels, the devils, the heavens and the earth?

It is related that in the reading of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud it is: "Are they a greater creation, or those whom We have counted (ʿaddadnā)?"

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqaʾ related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿Are they a greater creation, or those whom We have created?﴾ He said: the heavens, the earth and the mountains.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman related to us, from al-Dahhak that he read "Are they a greater creation, or those whom We have counted?" And in the reading of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud "ʿaddadnā" he says: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and Lord of the easts﴾ — he says: Are they a greater creation, or the heavens and the earth? He says: the heavens and the earth are a greater creation than them.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿So ask them: are they a greater creation, or those whom We have counted?﴾ — from the creation of the heavens and the earth. God said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ ... the verse.

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿So ask them: are they a greater creation?﴾ He said: He means the polytheists; ask them, are they a greater creation, ﴿or those whom We have created﴾.

As for His words ﴿Indeed, We created them from clay, sticky clay﴾:

He says: We created them from adhesive clay. He, may His praise be exalted, described it as "lazib" (sticky) because it is earth mixed with water. Likewise the creation of the son of Adam is from earth, water, fire and air. When earth is mixed with water it becomes sticky clay (ṭīn lāzib). The Arabs sometimes change this bāʾ into mīm, saying ṭīn lāzim (sticky clay). From this is the verse of al-Najashi al-Harithi:

"The meanness built a house, and its pillars became firm,
Upon you, sons of al-Najjar, a stricking, sticking blow."¹

And from lazib is the verse of Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan:

"They do not reckon good to be without evil after it,
Nor do they reckon evil to be a sticking blow."²

Sometimes they also replace the zay in lazib with a tāʾ, saying ṭīn lātib (sticky clay). It is mentioned that this is in the dialect of Qays. al-Farrāʾ claimed that Abu al-Jarrah recited to him:

"A headache, and the dislocation of bones, and lassitude,
And nausea with dizziness in the belly, are lātib (adhering)."³

Meaning: lāzim (adhering). The verb from lazib is lazaba, yalzubu, lazban and luzūban.⁴ Likewise from lātib: lataba, yaltubu, lutūban.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said things similar to what we have said on the meaning of ﴿lāzib﴾.

Those who said that:

* ʿUbayd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Jubayri related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us, saying: Muslim related to us, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning ﴿from sticky clay﴾: it is the good, fine, sticky clay.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Saʿid and ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim al-Batin, from Saʿid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: al-lazib: the good.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn Saʿid related to us, saying: Bishr ibn ʿUmara related to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: al-lazib: sticky, good.

* ʿAli related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning ﴿from sticky clay﴾: he says: adhering.

* Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His words ﴿Indeed, We created them from sticky clay﴾: from earth and water, which becomes clay that clings.

* Hannad related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from ʿIkrima, concerning ﴿Indeed, We created them from sticky clay﴾: al-lazib: sticky.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman related to us, from al-Dahhak, ﴿Indeed, We created them from sticky clay﴾, and al-lazib: good clay.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, God said ﴿Indeed, We created them from sticky clay﴾, and al-lazib: that which clings to the hand.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqaʾ related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿from sticky clay﴾: lazim (adhering).

* ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Amuli related to us, saying: Marwan ibn Muʿawiya related to us, saying: Juwaybir related to us, from al-Dahhak, concerning ﴿from sticky clay﴾: it is the adhering.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning ﴿Indeed, We created them from sticky clay﴾: al-lazib: that which sticks as if it were glue; that is lazib.

* *

As for His words ﴿Rather, you wonder, and they mock﴾:

The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the Kufan readers read ﴿Rather, I wonder (ʿajibtu), and they mock﴾ with a ḍammah on the tāʾ of ʿajibtu, meaning: rather, their taking partners for Me and their denying My revelation, while they mock, has become great in My estimation. The majority of the Medinan and Basran readers, and some Kufan readers, read ﴿Rather, you wonder (ʿajibta)﴾ with a fatḥah on the tāʾ, meaning: rather you wonder, O Muhammad, and they mock at this Qur'an.

The correct view on this is to say: these are two well-known readings among the readers of the regional centres, so whichever of them a reader recites, he is correct.

If someone says: how can a reader be correct with both when their meanings differ? It is said: although their meanings differ, each of their two meanings is sound. Muhammad has wondered at what God gave him of grace, and the people of polytheism mocked him; and our Lord has wondered at the enormity of what the polytheists said about God, and the polytheists mocked at what they said.

If he says: was the revelation with one of them or with both? It is said: the revelation was with both. If he says: how can a letter be revealed twice? It is said: it was not revealed twice; it was revealed once, but the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to recite with both readings, and this has a place where, God willing, we will fully explain it sufficiently.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Rather, you wonder, and they mock﴾: Muhammad (peace be upon him) wondered at this Qur'an when it was given to him, and the people of misguidance mocked it.

* *

As for His words ﴿Rather, you wonder, and they mock﴾:

The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the Kufan readers read ﴿Rather, I wonder (ʿajibtu), and they mock﴾ with a ḍammah on the tāʾ of ʿajibtu, meaning: rather, their taking partners for Me and their denying My revelation, while they mock, has become great in My estimation. The majority of the Medinan and Basran readers, and some Kufan readers, read ﴿Rather, you wonder (ʿajibta)﴾ with a fatḥah on the tāʾ, meaning: rather you wonder, O Muhammad, and they mock at this Qur'an.

The correct view on this is to say: these are two well-known readings among the readers of the regional centres, so whichever of them a reader recites, he is correct.

If someone says: how can a reader be correct with both when their meanings differ? It is said: although their meanings differ, each of their two meanings is sound. Muhammad has wondered at what God gave him of grace, and the people of polytheism mocked him; and our Lord has wondered at the enormity of what the polytheists said about God, and the polytheists mocked at what they said.

If he says: was the revelation with one of them or with both? It is said: the revelation was with both. If he says: how can a letter be revealed twice? It is said: it was not revealed twice; it was revealed once, but the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to recite with both readings, and this has a place where, God willing, we will fully explain it sufficiently.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Rather, you wonder, and they mock﴾: Muhammad (peace be upon him) wondered at this Qur'an when it was given to him, and the people of misguidance mocked it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verses 22–23:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, and their companions, and what they used to worship﴾ ﴿besides Allah, and lead them to the path of Hellfire﴾.

In this statement there is an omitted element, which is dispensed with by what has been mentioned, of what has been left out. It is: "Then it will be said: Gather those who did wrong." The meaning of that is: gather those who disbelieved in Allah in the world and disobeyed Him, and their spouses, and their followers, upon what they were upon of disbelief in Allah, and what they used to worship besides Allah of deities.

Those who engage in interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, regarding ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions﴾, he said: "their counterparts."

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions﴾, he says: "their peers."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions﴾, meaning: "their followers, and those who resemble them among the wrongdoers."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, who said: I asked Abu al-Aliyah about the saying of Allah: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions and what they used to worship besides Allah﴾, and he said: "Those who did wrong and their followers."

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 37, verses 28–30:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿They will say, "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right."﴾ [Q 37:28] ﴿They will say, "Rather, you were not believers."﴾ [Q 37:29] ﴿And we had no authority over you. Rather, you were a transgressing people."﴾ [Q 37:30]

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The humans said to the jinn: "Indeed, you, O jinn, used to come to us from the direction of religion and truth, and so you deceived us by the strongest means." Al-yamin (the right) means strength and power in the speech of the Arabs, and from it is the poet's saying:

"When a banner is raised for glory... ʿArabah meets it with al-yamin (strength)" [[This verse is among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (the University photocopy, folio 272). He said, regarding His words "you used to come to us from the right": he says: you used to come to us from the side of religion, that is, you came to us deceiving us by the strongest means, and "al-yamin" means by strength and power. I say: the verse is by al-Shammakh, praising ʿArabah al-Awsi, and before it is: "I saw ʿArabah al-Awsi rising to good deeds, without a rival." See (al-Lisan: y-m-n). He interpreted it as al-Farra' did. ʿArabah al-Awsi is the son of Aws ibn Qayzi. It is said that he is the one who said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the Battle of the Trench: "Indeed our houses are exposed." Al-Suhayli said in al-Rawd al-Unuf (2:190): ʿArabah al-Awsi was a chief, and he had no companionship (with the Prophet ﷺ); we mentioned him among those deemed too young on the day of Uhud, and he is the one about whom al-Shammakh said: "When a banner is raised for glory..." the verse.]]

That is: by strength and power.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAasim related to us, he said: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words "you used to come to us from the right": he said: from the truth; the disbelievers say it to the devils.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right": he said: The humans said to the jinn: "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right." He said: from the direction of good, so you forbade us from it and held us back from it.

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right": he said: you came to us from the side of truth, adorning falsehood for us and turning us away from truth.

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right": he said: The children of Adam said to the disbelieving devils: "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right." He said: you placed yourselves between us and good, and turned us away from Islam and faith, and from the good deed that Allah commanded.

* * *

As for His words ﴿They said, "Rather, you were not believers." And we had no authority over you﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The jinn answered the humans, saying: "Rather, you were not affirmers of the Oneness of Allah, and you were worshippers of idols."

﴿And we had no authority over you﴾ means: they said: "We had no proof against you, by which we might turn you away from faith and prevent you, because of it, from following the truth." ﴿Rather, you were a transgressing people﴾ means: they said to them: "Rather, you, O polytheists, were a people transgressing against Allah, exceeding to what was not permitted for you to exceed to, of disobedience to Allah and opposition to His command."

Ahl al-ta'wil said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: The jinn said to them: ﴿Rather, you were not believers﴾ up to ﴿a transgressing people﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 35–37:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, they were, when it was said to them, "There is no deity except Allah," arrogant﴾ [37:35] ﴿And they say, "Are we to leave our gods for a mad poet?"﴾ [37:36] ﴿Rather, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers﴾ [37:37].

His exalted remembrance says: Indeed, these polytheists, whose description is given in these verses, were in the world, when it was said to them, "Say: ﴿There is no deity except Allah,﴾" they were arrogant, meaning they magnified themselves against saying that and became proud. The words "say" have been omitted, being sufficiently indicated by the context.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said.

Among those who said this:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿when it was said to them, "There is no deity except Allah," they were arrogant﴾, he said: It refers specifically to the polytheists.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, they were, when it was said to them, "There is no deity except Allah," arrogant﴾, he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "Attend your dying, and prompt them to say 'There is no deity except Allah,' for they see and hear."

* *

And His saying ﴿And they say, "Are we to leave our gods for a mad poet?"﴾

His exalted remembrance says: These polytheists of Quraysh say, "Are we to abandon the worship of our gods for a mad poet?" meaning: are we to follow a mad poet. By this they meant the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), and [they meant that] we say: "There is no deity except Allah."

As follows:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And they say, "Are we to leave our gods for a mad poet?"﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ).

* *

And His saying ﴿Rather, he has brought the truth﴾

This is a report from Allah refuting the polytheists who said to the Prophet (ﷺ), "A mad poet." They lied; Muhammad is not as they described him, a mad poet. Rather, he is a Prophet of Allah who brought the truth from Him, which is the Qur'an that He revealed to him, and he confirmed the messengers who were before him.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said regarding this.

Among those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Rather, he has brought the truth﴾, [meaning] with the Qur'an, ﴿and confirmed the messengers﴾: i.e., he confirmed those messengers who came before him.

* *

His exalted remembrance says to these polytheists of Makkah, who said to Muhammad, "A mad poet": ﴿Indeed, you﴾, O polytheists, ﴿are going to taste the painful punishment﴾, the painful [punishment] in the Hereafter. ﴿And you will not be recompensed﴾, meaning: you will not be rewarded in the Hereafter when you taste the painful punishment there, ﴿except﴾ [the recompense of] ﴿what you used to do﴾ in the world, the disobedience of Allah.

* *

And His saying ﴿Except the chosen servants of Allah﴾

It means: except the servants of Allah whom He chose on the day He created them for His mercy, and for whom He decreed happiness in the Mother of the Book. Indeed, they do not taste the punishment, because they are people of obedience to Allah and people of faith in Him.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Except the chosen servants of Allah﴾, he said: This is an exception made by Allah.

* *

And His saying ﴿Those will have a known provision﴾

It means: these are the chosen servants of Allah, for whom is a known provision. That known provision is the fruits which Allah created for them in Paradise.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on Surah 37, verses 38–47:

Concerning the ta'wil (interpretation) of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Fruits, and they will be honoured, in Gardens of Bliss, upon couches facing one another. A cup from a flowing spring will be passed around among them, white, delicious to the drinkers, in which there is no ghawl (intoxicating harm), nor will they be drained by it.﴾

His saying ﴿fruits﴾ is in apposition to "provision known" (ar-rizq al-ma'lum), as an explanation of it, which is why it is in the nominative (marfu'). His saying ﴿and they will be honoured﴾ means: together with the known provision they have in Paradise, they will be honoured with the honour of God, with which God has honoured them.

﴿In Gardens of Bliss﴾ means: in the orchards of bliss.

﴿Upon couches facing one another﴾ means: that some of them face others, and no one looks at the back of another.

* *

As for His saying ﴿A cup from a flowing spring will be passed around among them﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the servants will circulate among them with a cup of wine that flows, visible to their eyes, not hidden.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning ﴿a cup from a flowing spring﴾, he said: a cup of flowing wine, and al-ma'in (the flowing spring) is the flowing (wine).

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salama ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, concerning His saying ﴿with a cup from a flowing spring﴾, he said: every cup in the Qur'an is wine.

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying ﴿with a cup from a flowing spring﴾, he said: the wine. * *

As for His saying ﴿white, delicious to the drinkers﴾:

By "white" is meant the cup. Because the cup is feminine, "white" is made feminine, and He did not say "white" in the masculine. It is related that in the recitation of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) the word is "yellow" (safra').

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying ﴿white﴾, al-Suddi said: in the recitation of Abdullah it is "yellow". * *

As for His saying ﴿in which there is no ghawl﴾:

It means: in this wine there is no ghawl, which is that it seizes their minds. That is: this wine does not take away the minds of its drinkers as the wines of the people of this world take them away when they drink and overindulge, as the poet said:

"The cup has never ceased to seize us, and to carry off the first and the foremost (of our wits)."

He said: when you place between the ghawl and the negation a preposition (lam or other particles of the genitive), it can only be in the nominative. He recited the verse in Lisan al-'Arab (root gh-w-l) from Abu 'Ubayda, with "al-khamr" in place of "al-kas" in one place. End.]]

The Arabs say: there is no ghaila, ghā'ila, or ghawl, with the same meaning. The word ghawl is in the nominative and is not put in the accusative after la, because a preposition has come between la and the noun (fiha). The Arabs do the same in negation: when a preposition comes between la and the noun, they make the noun nominative and do not make it accusative. The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed in the interpretation of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: there is no headache in it.

Those who said so:

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿la fiha ghawl﴾, he said: there is no headache in it.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: there is no harm in it, so that their stomachs complain of it.

Those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿la fiha ghawl﴾, he said: it is wine, in which there is no stomach-ache.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Waraqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿la fiha ghawl﴾, he said: stomach-ache.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿la fiha ghawl﴾: the ghawl is what gives pain to the stomach, and the drinker of wine here complains of his stomach.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning ﴿la fiha ghawl﴾, he says: there is no stomach-ache in it, nor headache.

Others said: the meaning is: they are not seized in their minds.

Those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿la fiha ghawl﴾, he said: it does not seize their minds.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: there is in it no harm or unpleasantness.

Those who said so:

* It was reported to me from Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'ida, from Isra'il, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His saying ﴿la fiha ghawl﴾, he said: no harm and no unpleasantness.

* Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Yaz'a narrated to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His saying ﴿la fiha ghawl﴾, he said: there is in it no harm and no unpleasantness.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: there is no sin in it.

Each of these sayings which we have mentioned has a valid aspect. The ghawl in the language of the Arabs is that which seizes a person and takes him away. Thus whoever is struck by something he dislikes, they coin this image for him, saying: "a ghawl seized so-and-so." So the one whose mind is taken away by drinking intoxicants, the one whose stomach complains from it, the one whose head aches from it, and the one who suffers any harm from it, all of them have been seized by a ghawl.

Since this is so, and God, may His remembrance be exalted, has negated from the drink of Paradise that there be in it any ghawl, then the more fitting description of it is what the Exalted said: ﴿in which there is no ghawl﴾, so that it generalizes by negating all the meanings of ghawl from it. The most comprehensive way of stating it is: there is no harm or unpleasantness in it for its drinkers, whether to body or mind, or anything else.

The readers (qurra') differed in the recitation of His saying ﴿nor will they be drained by it﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some of the readers of Kufa, recited ﴿yunzafun﴾ with a fatha on the za', meaning: nor will their minds be drained by drinking it. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited ﴿yunzifun﴾ with a kasra on the za', meaning: nor will their drink be exhausted from their drinking it.

The correct view on this is that both are well-known recitations, sound in meaning and not contradictory in sense. Whichever one the reader recites is correct, because the drink of the people of Paradise is never exhausted, nor does their drinking of it intoxicate them so as to take away their minds.

The interpreters differed on the meaning of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: their minds are not taken away.

Those who said so:

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿nor will they be drained by it﴾, he says: their minds are not taken away.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿nor will they be drained by it﴾, he said: they are not drained so as to lose their minds.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Waraqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿nor will they be drained by it﴾, he said: their minds are not taken away.

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying ﴿nor will they be drained by it﴾, he said: their minds are not drained.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿nor will they be drained by it﴾, he said: the minds are not drained.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿nor will they be drained by it﴾, he said: it does not overpower them over their minds.

This is because the Arabs say: "naza'a al-rajul fa-huwa manzuf" (the man was drained, so he is drained) when his mind has gone from intoxication, and "anzafa fa-huwa munzaf" (he was made drained), both forms being reported from them with the meaning of loss of the mind through intoxication. From the use of "inzaf" in the sense of the loss of the mind through intoxication is the saying of al-Abayrad:

"By my life, if you are drained or sober, how wretched are the boon companions you have been, O family of Abjar."

"You drank and voided yourselves, and your father was so too, when he drinks the cup he voids himself."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Those who said this:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿And with them will be those of restrained glances﴾, he said: "Not looking at anyone other than their husbands."

Al-Harith added in his narration: "They do not seek anyone other than them."

- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words ﴿And with them will be those of restrained glances﴾, he said: "They have restricted their sight and their hearts to their husbands, so they do not desire anyone else."

- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: It was also mentioned from Mansur, from Mujahid, the like of this.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the words of Allah ﴿those of restrained glances﴾, he said: "They do not look at anyone except their husbands; they have restricted their glances to their husbands, unlike the women of the people of this world."

* *

As for His words ﴿large, lovely eyes (in)﴾:

By "in" (ʿīn) is meant: those with beautiful, large eyes; it is the plural of ʿaynaʾ, and ʿaynaʾ is a woman with wide, large eyes, which is the most beautiful form of eyes.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words ﴿ʿīn﴾, he said: "Large of eyes."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿ʿīn﴾, he said: "The ʿaynaʾ is the one with large eyes."

- Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Sadafi al-Dimyati narrated to us, from Amr ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Karimah, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from his father, from Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that she said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, tell me about the words of Allah: ﴿Hur ʿīn﴾." He said: "The ʿīn are those with large eyes; the eyelid of the hurra' is like the wing of the eagle."

* *

As for His words ﴿As if they were protected eggs﴾:

The people of interpretation differed concerning what they were likened to in the eggs by this statement. Some of them said: They were likened to the inner part of the egg in whiteness, which is what lies inside the shell, because it has not been touched by anything.

Those who said this:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His words ﴿As if they were protected eggs﴾, he said: "As if they were the inner part of the egg."

- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿As if they were protected eggs﴾, he said: "The egg when it is peeled, before hands have touched it."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿As if they were protected eggs﴾, he said: "Hands have not passed over it nor touched it; they are likened to its whiteness."

Others said: Rather, they were likened to the egg that the bird incubates, which tends toward yellowness, so their whiteness in yellowness was likened to that.

Those who said this:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿As if they were protected eggs﴾, he said: "The egg which the feathers cover, like the eggs of the ostrich which the feathers have covered from the wind; it is white tending to yellow, so it seems to shine, and that is the protected (maknun)."

Others said: Rather, by "eggs" in this place is meant pearls, and they were likened to it in its whiteness and purity.

Those who said this:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿As if they were protected eggs﴾, he said: "The protected pearls."

"She is radiant, like a pearl of the oyster-shells, separated from a protected jewel."[[The verse is cited by Abu Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (Jami'ah manuscript, folio 209-1), where he said concerning the words of Allah "bayd maknun": "i.e., protected; every pearl, egg, or goods that you have guarded is maknun. And everything you conceal in yourself, you have akkantahu (concealed it). The poet said: 'And she is radiant...' the verse." End quote. He did not name the speaker, but the author (al-Tabari) named him.]]

And they say of everything the breasts conceal: akkantuhu, so it is mukann.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verses 54–57:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Would you like to look?"﴾ [54] ﴿So he looked and saw him in the midst of Hellfire.﴾ [55] ﴿He said, "By Allah, you were about to ruin me!﴾ [56] ﴿And if not for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forward [to punishment]."﴾ [57]

His saying, exalted is His mention: This believer who had entered Paradise said to his companions: ﴿"Would you like to look?"﴾ down into the Fire, "that I may see my companion who used to say to me: 'Are you truly among those who affirm that we will be resurrected after death?'"

* *

And His saying ﴿So he looked and saw him in the midst of Hellfire﴾

He says: he looked into the Fire and saw him in the middle of Hellfire. In the speech there is an omitted part, which is understood from the context, namely: they said, "Yes."

The people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding the interpretation of His saying ﴿So he looked and saw him in the midst of Hellfire﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿in the midst of Hellfire﴾, meaning: in the middle of Hellfire.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿in the midst of Hellfire﴾, meaning: in the middle of Hellfire.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Abbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿in the midst of Hellfire﴾, he says: in the middle of Hellfire.

- Ibn Sinan narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, he said: Abbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Hasan, and he mentioned the like of it.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, he said: Abu Hilal narrated to us, he said: Qatada narrated to us, regarding His saying ﴿midst of Hellfire﴾, he said: its middle.

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, he said: ﴿Would you like to look?﴾ He said: He asked his Lord to let him look. He said ﴿So he looked and saw him in the midst of Hellfire﴾: that is, in the middle of Hellfire.

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from Khulayd al-Asri, he said: Had Allah not made him recognize him, he would not have recognized him, for his features and his beauty had changed after him. It was mentioned to us that he looked and saw the skulls of the people, and said: ﴿By Allah, you were about to ruin me! And if not for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forward.﴾

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Wazir narrated to us, he said: Sufyan ibn Uyayna narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatada, from Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah, regarding His saying ﴿So he looked and saw him in the midst of Hellfire﴾, he said: By Allah, had he not recognized him, he would not have recognized him, for the Fire had changed his features and beauty.

- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿Would you like to look?﴾, he said: Ibn Abbas used to recite it: "Would you like to make me look? So he looked and saw him in the midst of Hellfire," he said: in the middle of Hellfire.

As for this reading which al-Suddi mentioned from Ibn Abbas, that he used to read "muttali'uni" in ﴿muttali'un﴾, if it is preserved from him, then it is among the irregular readings (shadhdh al-huruf). This is because the Arabs do not favor, with a pronoun attached to a verb-subject, the pronominal suffix in the form of an annexation (idafa), whether in plural or singular. They almost never say "anta mukallimuni" (you speak to me), nor "antuma mukallimani", nor "antum mukallimuni", nor "mukallimunni"; rather they say "anta mukallimi", "antuma mukallimay", and "antum mukallimi". If any one of them says that, he says it in error, having imagined: "anta tukallimuni", "antuma tukallimanni", "antum tukallimunni", as the poet said:

"I do not know, and my every assumption ... Will Shurahi hand me over to my people?"

The poet used "Muslimni" instead of "amuslimi", which is not the proper form of speech. Another said: "They are those who say the good and do it, when they fear from a new matter a great one." He did not say "al-fa'iluh", which is the proper form. The Arabs chose annexation with the pronoun because it mixes with what precedes it, so the two letters become like one letter; they preferred annexation with the pronoun, and they say "huma daribani Zaydan" and "dariba Zayd", because Zayd, when it is apparent, does not mix with what precedes it, since it is not a single letter, whereas the pronoun is a letter. As for His saying "fa-talla'a", it is in the sense of "he was made to do that", as you say: "da'a fa-ujiba, ya hadha" (he called, so he was answered, O you). The meaning would be: "Would you like to look? [So] I will look," making it accusative in response to the fa'.

As for when the speech is apparent and not attached to the subject, they sometimes annex and sometimes do not: one says "hadha mukallimu akhika" and "mukallimu akhika", "hadhan mukallima akhika" and "mukallimani akhaka", "ha'ula'i mukallimu akhika" and "mukallimuna akhaka". The annexation with the attached pronoun to a subject is preferred only because the two letters join together through the attachment of one to the other, like a single letter.

* *

And His saying ﴿By Allah, you were about to ruin me!﴾

He says: when he saw his companion in the Fire, he said: By Allah, you were about to destroy me in the world by your turning me away from belief in resurrection, reward and punishment.

The people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿you were about to ruin me﴾, he said: to destroy me. It is said from it: "Ardá Fulan Fulanan" when he destroyed him, and "Radiya Fulan" when he perished, as al-A'sha said:

"Did you fear for me destruction in the journey, and how many a one who perished did not leave his family?"

Al-Farra said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an: "Would you like to look?": This is a man from the people of Paradise, who had a brother from the people of disbelief, and he loved to see his place, so Allah permitted him, and he looked into the Fire and addressed him, and when he saw him he said, "By Allah, you were about to ruin me." In the reading of Abd Allah, that is Ibn Mas'ud: "You were about to lead me astray, and if not for the mercy of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forward," meaning: with you in the Fire, brought forward.

He means by his saying "wa-kam min rad": how many a one perished.

* *

And His saying ﴿And if not for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forward﴾

He says: And if not that Allah had bestowed upon me His guidance and granted me success in belief in resurrection after death, I would have been among those brought forward with you in the punishment of Allah.

As:

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿I would have been among those brought forward﴾: that is, in the punishment of Allah.

He, the Exalted, says, relating the words of this believer whom Allah granted what He granted of His honour in His Garden, out of joy at what He had bestowed upon him therein: ﴿Is it not that we shall not die, except our first death﴾ — meaning: Is it not that we shall not die other than our first death, the one in this world? ﴿And we shall not be punished﴾ — meaning: and we shall not be punished after our entry into the Garden. ﴿Indeed, this is the great triumph﴾ — meaning: indeed, this which Allah has given us of honour in the Garden, that we will not be punished nor die, is the great deliverance from what we used to fear in the world of Allah's punishment, and the attainment of what we used to hope for in the world through our faith and our obedience to our Lord.

As narrated:

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Is it not that we shall not die﴾ up to His saying ﴿the great triumph﴾, he said: This is the statement of the people of the Garden.

* *

And His saying ﴿For the like of this let the workers work﴾

He, the Exalted, says: for the like of what I have given these believers of honour in the Hereafter, let those who work in this world work for their own souls, so that they may attain what these attained through obedience to their Lord.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 62–66:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of al-Zaqqum?﴾ ﴿Indeed, We made it a trial for the wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire.﴾ ﴿Its emergent is as if it were the heads of devils.﴾ ﴿Indeed, they will eat from it and fill with it their bellies.﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: Is this which I have given to these believers, whose qualities You have been described, of My honor in Paradise, and the provision I have bestowed on them therein of delight, better, or what I have prepared for the people of the Fire of al-Zaqqum? By "nuzul" (welcome, provision) is meant the bounty. It has two forms: nuzl and nuzul. It is said of food that has yield: it is food that has nuzl and nuzul.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿or the tree of al-Zaqqum﴾

It is mentioned that when Allah sent down this verse, the polytheists said: How can a tree grow in the Fire, when the Fire burns trees? So Allah said: ﴿Indeed, We made it a trial for the wrongdoers﴾, meaning these polytheists who said what they said about it. Then He informed them of the description of this tree, saying: ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire﴾.

And the people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of al-Zaqqum﴾ up to ﴿from the root of Hellfire﴾: When the tree of al-Zaqqum was mentioned, the wrongdoers were tempted, and they said: Your companion tells you that in the Fire there is a tree, and the Fire consumes trees. So Allah sent down what you hear: "Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire," nourished by fire and created from it.

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Abu Jahl said when "Indeed, the tree of al-Zaqqum" was revealed: You know it in the speech of the Arabs. I will bring it to you. He called a slave-girl and said: Bring me dates and butter. Then he said: Help yourselves, and eat zaqqum, for this is the zaqqum with which Muhammad threatens you. So Allah revealed its explanation: ﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of al-Zaqqum? Indeed, We made it a trial for the wrongdoers﴾, meaning Abu Jahl and his companions.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We made it a trial for the wrongdoers﴾: It is the saying of Abu Jahl: "Zaqqum is only dates and butter; I will eat it (tazaqqamuh)."

* *

As for His saying ﴿Its emergent is as if it were the heads of devils﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: The emergent of this tree, meaning the tree of al-Zaqqum, in its ugliness and repulsiveness, is as if it were the heads of devils in their ugliness.

It is mentioned that this is in the reading of Abdullah: "Indeed, it is a tree growing from the root of the Hellfire."

As:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Its emergent is as if it were the heads of devils﴾: He likened it to that.

If someone says: What is the meaning of likening the emergent of this tree to the heads of devils in ugliness, when we have no knowledge of the extent of the ugliness of the heads of devils? Something is compared to another thing only to make it known by the one who makes the comparison, due to the close resemblance of one of the two to the other, while the one being compared knows both things, or one of them. And it is known that the polytheists addressed by this verse did not know the tree of al-Zaqqum, nor the heads of devils, nor had they seen either of them, nor either one of them?

It is said to him: As for the tree of al-Zaqqum, Allah, may He be exalted, has described it to them and explained it until they knew what it is and what its description is, saying to them: (It is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire; its emergent is as if it were the heads of devils), so He did not leave them in blindness about it. As for His likening its emergent to the heads of devils, I say that each of these has an understandable meaning. One: that it is like the heads of devils in the manner in which the addressees of the verse commonly use the phrase among themselves, for people's usage has long been that when one wants to exaggerate in denouncing something, he says: "It is like a devil." That is one of the sayings. The second: that it is like the head of a well-known snake among the Arabs called a shaytan, a snake with a mane, said to be of ugly face and appearance, and it is this that the rajiz meant by his saying:

"Angry-woman swears whenever I swear... like the devil of al-Hammat, I am more knowing."

[These two lines are from a rajaz meter, recited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (University of Jordan manuscript 273) when explaining His saying, "as if they were the heads of devils." He said: In Arabic there are three aspects: one, that you liken its emergent in its ugliness to the heads of devils, because it is described as ugly, as though it were unseen, and you say to a man "like a devil" when you find him repulsive. Another: the Arabs call some snakes a shaytan, a snake with a mane; a poet said, dispraising a wife of his: "Angry-woman swears..." It is also said that it is an ugly verse called "the heads of devils." The three aspects return to one meaning of ugliness. End. In Lisan al-'Arab (ʿ-n-j-r-d): al-Azhari, citing al-Farra': "an 'anjarad woman" is wicked, of bad character; he recited the verse of evidence. Another said: "an 'anjarad woman" means shrewish. In Lisan (h-m-t), from al-Jawhari: al-Hammat is the dried-up vegetation of vipers, which snakes frequent; it is said "shaytan hammat," as one says "a wolf angry" and "a ram of breeding." Al-Azhari said: the Arabs say of a kind of snake "shaytan al-hammat." It is said that hammat in the dialect of Hudhayl is a large tree that grows in their lands, which snakes frequent; hammat is specifically the chaff of maize, from Abu Hanifa. End.]

It is also narrated as "'ujayyiz." The third: that it is like a known plant called the heads of devils, said to have an ugly head. ﴿So indeed they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it﴾. He, may He be exalted, says: Indeed these polytheists, for whom Allah made this tree a trial, will eat from this tree, which is the tree of al-Zaqqum, and fill their bellies with its zaqqum.

One: that it is like the heads of devils in the manner in which the addressees of the verse commonly use the phrase among themselves, for people's usage has long been that when one wants to exaggerate in denouncing something, he says: "It is like a devil." That is one of the sayings. The second: that it is like the head of a well-known snake among the Arabs called a shaytan, a snake with a mane, said to be of ugly face and appearance, and it is this that the rajiz meant by his saying:

"Angry-woman swears whenever I swear... like the devil of al-Hammat, I am more knowing."

He, may He be exalted, says: Is this which I have given to these believers, whose qualities You have been described, of My honor in Paradise, and the provision I have bestowed on them therein of delight, better, or what I have prepared for the people of the Fire of al-Zaqqum? By "nuzul" (welcome, provision) is meant the bounty. It has two forms: nuzl and nuzul. It is said of food that has yield: it is food that has nuzl and nuzul.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿or the tree of al-Zaqqum﴾

It is mentioned that when Allah sent down this verse, the polytheists said: How can a tree grow in the Fire, when the Fire burns trees? So Allah said: ﴿Indeed, We made it a trial for the wrongdoers﴾, meaning these polytheists who said what they said about it. Then He informed them of the description of this tree, saying: ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire﴾.

And the people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of al-Zaqqum﴾ up to ﴿from the root of Hellfire﴾: When the tree of al-Zaqqum was mentioned, the wrongdoers were tempted, and they said: Your companion tells you that in the Fire there is a tree, and the Fire consumes trees. So Allah sent down what you hear: "Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire," nourished by fire and created from it.

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Abu Jahl said when "Indeed, the tree of al-Zaqqum" was revealed: You know it in the speech of the Arabs. I will bring it to you. He called a slave-girl and said: Bring me dates and butter. Then he said: Help yourselves, and eat zaqqum, for this is the zaqqum with which Muhammad threatens you. So Allah revealed its explanation: ﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of al-Zaqqum? Indeed, We made it a trial for the wrongdoers﴾, meaning Abu Jahl and his companions.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We made it a trial for the wrongdoers﴾: It is the saying of Abu Jahl: "Zaqqum is only dates and butter; I will eat it (tazaqqamuh)."

* *

As for His saying ﴿Its emergent is as if it were the heads of devils﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: The emergent of this tree, meaning the tree of al-Zaqqum, in its ugliness and repulsiveness, is as if it were the heads of devils in their ugliness.

It is mentioned that this is in the reading of Abdullah: "Indeed, it is a tree growing from the root of the Hellfire."

As:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Its emergent is as if it were the heads of devils﴾: He likened it to that.

If someone says: What is the meaning of likening the emergent of this tree to the heads of devils in ugliness, when we have no knowledge of the extent of the ugliness of the heads of devils? Something is compared to another thing only to make it known by the one who makes the comparison, due to the close resemblance of one of the two to the other, while the one being compared knows both things, or one of them. And it is known that the polytheists addressed by this verse did not know the tree of al-Zaqqum, nor the heads of devils, nor had they seen either of them, nor either one of them?

It is said to him: As for the tree of al-Zaqqum, Allah, may He be exalted, has described it to them and explained it until they knew what it is and what its description is, saying to them: (It is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire; its emergent is as if it were the heads of devils), so He did not leave them in blindness about it. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 67–70:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then indeed for them over it is a mixture of boiling water﴾ [37:67]. Then indeed for these polytheists, upon what they eat of this tree, the tree of Zaqqum, is a shawb (mixture), and shawb is the mixing, from the expression of the Arabs: "shaba fulan ta'amahu" (so-and-so mixed his food), "fahuwa yashubuhu shawban wa-shiyaban" (and he mixes it, a mixing and a mixing). ﴿From boiling water﴾. And the hamim (boiling water) is the heated water, which has been heated until its heat has ended; its origin is the passive participle (maf'ul) that has been turned into the form fa'il.

Those who explain the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Then indeed for them over it is a mixture of boiling water﴾, he said: it means a mixing (lamazjan).

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Then indeed for them over it is a mixture of boiling water﴾, he means: the drinking of boiling water over the Zaqqum.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿Then indeed for them over it is a mixture of boiling water﴾, he said: a mixing (mizajan) of boiling water.

- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Then indeed for them over it is a mixture of boiling water﴾, he said: the shawb is the mixing, and it is the blending (mazj).

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Then indeed for them over it is a mixture of boiling water﴾, he said: boiling water is mixed for them with ghasaq, from what their eyes flow with, and pus from their discharge and their blood, from what comes out of their bodies.

* *

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Then indeed for them over it is a mixture of boiling water﴾, he said: it means a mixing (lamazjan).

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Then indeed for them over it is a mixture of boiling water﴾, he means: the drinking of boiling water over the Zaqqum.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿Then indeed for them over it is a mixture of boiling water﴾, he said: a mixing (mizajan) of boiling water.

- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Then indeed for them over it is a mixture of boiling water﴾, he said: the shawb is the mixing, and it is the blending (mazj).

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Then indeed for them over it is a mixture of boiling water﴾, he said: boiling water is mixed for them with ghasaq, from what their eyes flow with, and pus from their discharge and their blood, from what comes out of their bodies.

* *

And His saying ﴿Then indeed their return is surely to the Hellfire﴾ [37:68].

He, exalted is He, says: Then indeed their resort and their destination is surely to the Hellfire.

As:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿Then indeed their return is surely to the Hellfire﴾, he said: they are in toil and torment from the fire of Hell, and he recited this verse: ﴿They will go around between it and boiling water, intensely hot﴾ [55:44].

- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿Then indeed their return is surely to the Hellfire﴾, he said: in the recitation of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): "Then indeed their turning back is surely to the Hellfire." Abdullah used to say: By He in whose hand is my soul, the day of resurrection will not reach midday until the people of Paradise take their midday rest in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire. Then he said: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that day are better in resting place and finer in resort﴾ [25:24].

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Then indeed their return is surely to the Hellfire﴾, he said: their death. [[Possibly: their abode or their final destination.]]

* *

And His saying ﴿Indeed, they found their fathers astray﴾ [37:69].

He says: Indeed these polytheists, who, when it is said to them, "Say: There is no god but Allah," become arrogant, found their fathers in error from the right path, not following the clear road of truth.

﴿So they, upon their traces, are rushed﴾ [37:70]. He says: So these are driven swiftly along their path, to follow their traces and their way. It is said of it: "Ahra'a fulan" (so-and-so was hastened) when he walks with a hurried pace, which has a resemblance to trembling.

Those who explain the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, they found their fathers astray﴾, he said: meaning they found their fathers.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Indeed, they found their fathers﴾: meaning they found their fathers.

And in agreement with what we have said regarding yuhra'un (are rushed) as well, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿So they, upon their traces, are rushed﴾, he said: like the manner of hurrying (harwalah).

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿So they, upon their traces, are rushed﴾: meaning they are hastened with great haste in that.

- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿are rushed﴾, he said: they hasten.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿they are rushed to it﴾, he said: they hurry to it.

The Exalted says: And indeed, O Muhammad, before your people from Quraysh, most of the earlier nations had gone astray from the straight path and the road of truth. ﴿And indeed We sent among them warners﴾, meaning: And indeed We sent among the nations that passed before your community and before your people who deny you, warners, to warn them of Our punishment for their disbelief in Us. They denied them and did not accept their advice, so We brought down upon them Our punishment and Our retribution. ﴿So observe how was the end of those who were warned﴾, meaning: Reflect and consider how the outcome was for those whom Our prophets warned, where their affair ended, and what their disbelief in Allah brought upon them. Did We not destroy them, making them a lesson for the servants and an admonition for those after them?

* *

Regarding His words ﴿except the chosen servants of Allah﴾:

The Exalted says: So observe how was the end of those who were warned, except the servants of Allah whom We purified for faith in Allah and His messengers. He made an exception of the servants of Allah from those who were warned, because the meaning of the statement is: So observe how We destroyed those who were warned, except the believing servants of Allah. Therefore their exception from them is fitting.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) said the same as what we have said concerning His words ﴿except the chosen servants of Allah﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verses 75–77:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And Noah had certainly called Us, and We are the best to respond.  And We saved him and his family from the great distress. And We made his descendants the survivors.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Noah had certainly called upon Us, by asking Us to destroy his people, and so he said: ﴿My Lord, indeed I have invited my people night and day, but my invitation has increased them not except in flight... up to His words, (My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant).﴾ His words ﴿So We are the best to respond﴾ mean: We were the best of responders when he called upon Us, so We answered his supplication and destroyed his people. ﴿And We saved him and his family﴾ means: the family of Noah who boarded the ship with him. We have already mentioned them earlier, and we explained the scholars' differences regarding their number.

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And Noah had certainly called Us, and We are the best to respond﴾, he said: Allah answered him.

* *

And His words ﴿from the great distress﴾

He says: from the harm and adversity he suffered from the disbelievers, and from the distress of the Flood and drowning by which the people of Noah were destroyed.

As follows:

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And We saved him and his family from the great distress﴾, he said: from drowning.

* *

And His words ﴿And We made his descendants the survivors﴾

He says: And We made the descendants of Noah those who remained on the earth after the destruction of his people. This is because all people from after the destruction of Noah until today are none other than the descendants of Noah: the Persians and the Arabs are the sons of Sam ibn Noah, the Turks, the Slavs and the Khazars are the sons of Yafith ibn Noah, and the Sudanese are the sons of Ham ibn Noah. Reports have come to this effect, and the scholars have said so.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ashmah narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Samurah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His words ﴿And We made his descendants the survivors﴾, he said: "Sam, Ham and Yafith."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And We made his descendants the survivors﴾, he said: So all people are from the descendants of Noah.

* Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We made his descendants the survivors﴾, he said: None remained except the descendants of Noah.
