Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verses 78–82:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾ [78] ﴿Peace be upon Noah among the worlds﴾ [79] ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾ [80] ﴿Indeed, he was among Our believing servants﴾ [81] ﴿Then We drowned the others﴾ [82]

By His saying ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: We preserved for him, that is for Noah, a good mention and a fine praise among the later generations, meaning among those who came after him of mankind, who mention him by it.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾: he said, "He is mentioned with goodness."

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾: he said, "We made him a tongue of truthfulness for all the prophets."

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾: he said, "God preserved for him a good praise among the later generations."

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾: he said, "The good praise."

* * *

As for His words ﴿Peace be upon Noah among the worlds﴾:

It means: a security from God for Noah among the worlds, that anyone should mention him with evil; and "peace" (salam) is in the nominative case, governed by "upon" (ala). Some of the grammarians of Arabic from Kufa said: its meaning is, "And We left upon him among the later generations, ﴿Peace upon Noah﴾," meaning: We left upon him this statement, just as you say, "I read from the Qur'an ﴿All praise is for God, Lord of the worlds﴾," so the sentence has the sense of the accusative, and you raise it with the lam; likewise "peace upon Noah" you raise with "upon," though it is in the sense of the accusative. He said: Had it been "We left upon him peace," it would have been correct.

* * *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, just as We did with Noah, a recompense to him for his obedience to Us and his patience over the harm of his people in Our pleasure, ﴿And We saved him and his family from the great distress﴾, ﴿and We made his descendants the survivors﴾, and We preserved for him a praise among the later generations. ﴿Thus do We reward﴾ those who do good, who obey Us, submit to Our command, and endure harm for Our sake.

* * *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, he was among Our believing servants﴾:

It means: Indeed Noah was among Our servants who believed in Us, affirmed Our oneness, sincerely devoted worship to Us, and singled Us out for divinity.

As for His words ﴿Then We drowned the others﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Then We drowned, when We saved Noah and his family from the great distress, those of his people who remained.

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Then We drowned the others﴾: he said, "God saved him and those with him in the ship, and drowned the rest of his people."

"Ḥuṣayn wished that Jidhā'ah would be lords, but Ḥuṣayn became humbled and subdued (aqhara)."

[Editorial note: the line is by al-Mukhabbal al-Sa'di satirising al-Zibriqan; al-Farra' cites it in support of al-A'mash's reading.]

Then he said: "aqhara" means he came to a state of subjugation, and it is only "quhira"; the people then recited "yazifūna" with a fatha on the yā' and a kasra on the zāy. Some readers recited "yazafūna" with lightening (takhfīf) of the fā', as if it were from "wazafa yazifu". It is related of al-Kisa'i that he did not know it, and al-Farra' said: I do not know it either, unless it is a dialect I have not heard.

It is related from Mujahid that he used to say: al-wazf is al-naslān (a gait of ambling).

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿ilayhi yazifūn﴾, he said: al-wazīf is al-naslān.

The correct reading in this matter, in our view, is the reading of the one who recited it with a fatha on the yā' and a shaddah on the fā', because that is the sound and well-known usage of the Arabs, and the reading of the eloquent readers.

The people of interpretation differed concerning its meaning. Some said: its meaning is that the people of Abraham came to Abraham running (yajrūn).

Those who said that:

* 'Ali related to me, who said: Abu Salih related to us, who said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿Then they came hastening towards him﴾: they came to him running.

Others said: they came to him walking (yamshūn).

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words ﴿Then they came hastening towards him﴾, he said: walking.

Others said: its meaning is: they came hastening (yastaʿjilūn).

Those who said that:

* Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, from his father, concerning ﴿Then they came hastening towards him﴾: he said: hastening; and he said: yazaff means yastaʿjil (to hasten).

* * *

As for His words ﴿He said: "Do you worship what you carve?"﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Abraham said to his people: Do you worship, O people, what you carve with your hands of idols?

As related:

* Bishr related to me, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿He said: "Do you worship what you carve?"﴾: the idols.

* * *

As for His words ﴿while Allah created you and what you make!﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, reporting the speech of Abraham to his people: "And Allah created you, O people, and what you make." Regarding His words ﴿and what you make﴾ there are two possible meanings. One is that "mā" here is a verbal noun (maṣdar), so the sense of the statement becomes: Allah created you and your work.

The other is that it means "alladhī" (that which), so the sense becomes: Allah created you and that which you make: that is, that from which you make the idols, namely the wood, the copper, and the materials from which they used to carve their idols.

This second meaning is what Qatadah intended, God willing, in his statement reported by Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And Allah created you and what you make﴾: "with your hands".

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verses 97–100:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿They said, "Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire."﴾ (97) ﴿And they intended a plot against him, but We made them the lowest.﴾ (98) ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ (99) ﴿"My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous."﴾ (100)

His, may He be remembered, saying: The people of Abraham said, when Abraham said to them: ﴿Do you worship what you carve, while God created you and what you make?﴾ "Build for Abraham a structure." It is mentioned that they built for him a structure resembling a furnace (tannur), then they carried the firewood to it and kindled it upon him, ﴿so throw him into the blazing fire.﴾ The jahim (blazing fire) in the Arabic language is: the embers of fire piled upon one another, and fire upon fire.

* *

And His saying ﴿they intended a plot against him﴾

His, may He be remembered, saying: The people of Abraham intended a plot, and that was what they intended of burning him with fire. God says: ﴿So We made them﴾, meaning, We made the people of Abraham ﴿the lowest﴾, meaning the most humiliated in argument, and We gave Abraham victory over them through argument, and We rescued him from the plot they intended against him.

As:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿they intended a plot against him, but We made them the lowest﴾, he said: He did not debate with them after that until He destroyed them.

* *

And His saying ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾

He says: And Abraham said, when God granted him victory over his people and saved him from their plot: ﴿Indeed, I am going to my Lord﴾, meaning: I am migrating from the land of my people to God, that is, to the holy land, and separating from them, withdrawing from them to worship God.

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾: going with his deeds, his heart, and his intention.

Others said concerning this: Abraham only said ﴿Indeed, I am going to my Lord﴾ when they intended to throw him into the fire.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abu Dawud narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Sulayman ibn Surad say: When they intended to throw Abraham into the fire, ﴿he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ They gathered the firewood, and an old woman came carrying firewood on her back. She was asked: Where are you going? She said: I want to go to this man who is being thrown into the fire. When he was thrown into it, he said: "Sufficient for me is God; upon Him I have relied," or he said: "Sufficient for us is God, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." He said: God said: ﴿O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham.﴾ He said: The son of Lut, or the son of the brother of Lut, said: The fire did not burn him for my sake, and there was kinship between them. So God sent upon him a flame of fire and it burned him.

I chose the view I have stated, because God, blessed and exalted, mentioned his account and the account of his people in another place, and He reported that when He rescued him from what his people sought to burn him with, he said: ﴿Indeed, I am migrating to my Lord﴾. The people of interpretation explained that its meaning is: I am migrating to the land of Syria. Likewise His saying ﴿Indeed, I am going to my Lord﴾, since it is like His saying ﴿Indeed, I am migrating to my Lord﴾. And His saying ﴿He will guide me﴾ means: He will keep me firm upon the guidance that I have perceived, and help me upon it.

* *

And His saying ﴿"My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous."﴾

This is Abraham's request of his Lord that He grant him a righteous son. He says: He said: O my Lord, grant me from You a son who will be among the righteous who obey You and do not disobey You, and who act righteously in the earth and do not corrupt.

As:

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous﴾, he said: a righteous son.

He said "from among the righteous" and did not say "a righteous one from among the righteous," relying on what is mentioned to indicate what is omitted, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿and they were among the abstainers (zahidin)﴾, meaning "abstainers from among the abstainers."

He said, "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast."﴾ [37:102]

His remembrance, exalted is He, says: We gave Abraham the good news of a forbearing boy, meaning a boy who possesses forbearance (ḥilm) when he grows up. As for in his infancy in the cradle, he is not described by that. It is mentioned that the boy whom Allah gave Abraham the good news of was Isaac.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yazid, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿So We gave him the good news of a forbearing boy﴾ He said: He is Isaac.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah (﴿So We gave him the good news of a forbearing boy﴾): He gave the good news of Isaac. He said: Forbearance was not ascribed to anyone other than Isaac and Abraham.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion﴾

He says: When the boy whom Abraham was given the good news of reached, along with Abraham, the work, which is the exertion (saʿy), and that is when he was able to help him in his work.

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion﴾: He says: the work.

* al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: When he grew up, when he reached his exertion.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid: ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion﴾ He said: The exertion of Abraham.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid: ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion﴾: The exertion of Abraham.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion﴾: Here, exertion (saʿy) means worship.

Others said: The meaning of that is: When he walked with Abraham.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah (﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion﴾): That is, when he walked with his father.

* *

And His saying: ﴿He said, "O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you"﴾

His remembrance, exalted is He, says: Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, said to his son: ﴿O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you﴾. It is mentioned that when the angels gave Abraham the good news of Isaac as a son, he vowed that if Sarah bore him, he would make him a sacrifice for Allah. So when Isaac reached the age of exertion with his father, Abraham was shown in a dream, and it was said to him: "Fulfil your vow to Allah," and the dreams of the prophets are certainty. Therefore he proceeded upon what he saw in the dream, and his son Isaac said what he said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Gabriel said to Sarah: "Rejoice at a son named Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob." She struck her forehead in wonder, and that is His saying ﴿and she struck her face﴾ and ﴿She said, "Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is an amazing thing!"﴾ up to His saying ﴿Praiseworthy and Glorious﴾. Sarah said to Gabriel: "What is the sign of that?" So he took a dry stick in his hand, twisted it between his fingers, and it turned green and stirred. Abraham said: "Then it is for Allah a sacrifice." When Isaac grew up, Abraham was visited in sleep, and it was said to him: "Fulfil your vow that you vowed, that Allah has granted you a boy from Sarah, that you sacrifice him." He said to Isaac: "Set out, let us offer a sacrifice to Allah," and he took a knife and a rope and set out with him until, when he had taken him between the mountains, the boy said to him: "O father, where is your offering?" ﴿He said, "O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you. So see what you think." He said, "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast."﴾ Then Isaac said to him: "O father, tighten my bonds so that I do not thrash about, and keep your garments away from me so that nothing of my blood splashes on them, lest Sarah see it and grieve, and hasten the passage of the knife over my throat, so that death will be easier for me. When you come to Sarah, convey my greetings to her." Abraham came toward him, kissing him, while he had bound him, and he was weeping and Isaac was weeping, until the tears pooled under Isaac's cheek. Then he drew the knife across his throat, but the knife did not cut, and Allah struck a plate of copper on Isaac's throat. When he saw that, he struck him on the forehead and cut at the nape. That is His saying ﴿So when they had both submitted﴾, meaning: they both submitted the matter to Allah, ﴿and he put him down upon his forehead﴾. Then he was called: "O Abraham, ﴿you have fulfilled the vision﴾" in truth. He turned and behold, there was a ram; he took it and released his son. He fell upon his son, kissing him, and said: "Today, O my son, you have been given to me." Therefore Allah says: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾. He returned to Sarah and informed her of the news, and Sarah became distressed and said: "O Abraham, you wanted to slaughter my son and did not inform me!"

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you﴾: He said: The dreams of the prophets are true; when they see something in a dream, they act upon it.

* Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, who said: The dreams of the prophets are revelation, then he recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you﴾.

* *

His saying ﴿So see what you think﴾

The readers differed in reading His saying ﴿what you think﴾. The majority of the readers of Madinah and Basrah, and some readers of Kufah, read it as ﴿مَاذَا تَرَى﴾ with a fatha on the tā', meaning: "what do you command" or "see what it is you command." The majority of the readers of Kufah read "مَاذَا تُرَى" with a ḍammah on the tā', meaning: "what do you indicate," and "what do you see of your patience or your distress at the slaughter?"

The reading most correct in my view among the two is the reading of the one who reads ﴿مَاذَا تَرَى﴾ with a fatha on the tā', meaning: "what opinion do you hold?"

If someone says: Would Abraham consult his son about proceeding with the command of Allah and submitting to His obedience? It is said: That was not consultation from him with his son regarding obedience to Allah, but it was from him in order to know what resolve his son had: whether he was patient in the matter of Allah's command to the same degree as he was, so that he would be pleased by that or not; and he was in all states proceeding in obedience to Allah's command.

* *

His saying ﴿He said, "O my father, do as you are commanded"﴾

His remembrance, exalted is He, says: Isaac said to his father: "O father, do what your Lord commands you regarding my slaughter." ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast﴾, meaning: you will find me, if Allah wills, patient among the patient regarding what our Lord commands us. He said "do what you are commanded" and did not say "what you are commanded with," because the meaning is: do the command which you are ordered. It is mentioned that this is in the reading of ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud): "Indeed I have seen in a dream: do what I have been commanded."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verses 101–102:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We gave him the good news of a forbearing boy﴾ [37:101] ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion, he said, "O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you, so see what you think." He said, "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast."﴾ [37:102]

His remembrance, exalted is He, says: We gave Abraham the good news of a forbearing boy, meaning a boy who possesses forbearance (ḥilm) when he grows up. As for in his infancy in the cradle, he is not described by that. It is mentioned that the boy whom Allah gave Abraham the good news of was Isaac.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yazid, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿So We gave him the good news of a forbearing boy﴾ He said: He is Isaac.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah (﴿So We gave him the good news of a forbearing boy﴾): He gave the good news of Isaac. He said: Forbearance was not ascribed to anyone other than Isaac and Abraham.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion﴾

He says: When the boy whom Abraham was given the good news of reached, along with Abraham, the work, which is the exertion (saʿy), and that is when he was able to help him in his work.

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

* ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion﴾: He says: the work.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion﴾: When he grew up until he reached the exertion of Abraham in work.

* al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: When he grew up, when he reached his exertion.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid: ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion﴾ He said: The exertion of Abraham.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid: ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion﴾: The exertion of Abraham.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion﴾: Here, exertion (saʿy) means worship.

Others said: The meaning of that is: When he walked with Abraham.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah (﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion﴾): That is, when he walked with his father.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me, saying: Thabit ibn Muhammad related to us, and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Salih related to us, both of them saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, concerning His saying ﴿So when they had both submitted﴾, he said: They agreed upon one matter.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, from Yazid, from Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿So when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead﴾, he said: Both of them submitted together to the command of God, and the boy was content to be slaughtered, and the father was content to slaughter him. He said: "O father, throw me down on my face so that you do not look at me and have mercy on me, and I do not look at the blade and become distressed; but insert the blade from beneath me, and proceed with the command of God." That is His saying ﴿So when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead﴾. When he did that, ﴿And We called to him, "O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision." Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good.﴾

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿So when they had both submitted﴾, he said: This one submitted himself to God, and this one, his son, submitted to God.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿So when they had both submitted﴾, he said: They submitted to what they were commanded.

Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿So when they had both submitted﴾, he says: They submitted to the command of God.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, ﴿So when they had both submitted﴾: that is, Abraham submitted to slaughtering him when he was commanded to do so, and his son submitted to being patient with it, when he knew that God had commanded that concerning him.

* *

And His saying ﴿and he put him down upon his forehead﴾

He says: and he threw him down upon the forehead (lil-jabin). The two jabinan are what lies to the right and to the left of the brow (al-jabhah); the face has two jabinan, and the jabhah is between them.

The people of interpretation said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿and he put him down upon his forehead﴾, he said: He placed his face on the ground, and said: "Do not slaughter me while you look at my face, perhaps you will have mercy on me, and do not finish me off; tie my hand to my neck, then place my face on the ground."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿and he put him down upon his forehead﴾: that is, he overturned him onto his mouth and took the blade ﴿And We called to him, "O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision"﴾ until ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿and he put him down upon his forehead﴾, he said: He made him lie on his forehead.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and he put him down upon his forehead﴾, he said: His brow; he took his brow in order to slaughter him.

Ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Hammad, from Abu Asim al-Ghanawi, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ibn Abbas said: When Abraham was commanded with the rites, Satan appeared to him at al-Mas'a, and raced him, and Abraham outran him. Then Gabriel took him to the Jamrat al-Aqabah, and Satan appeared to him, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he went away. Then he appeared to him at the middle jamrah, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he went away. Then he put him down upon the forehead, and Isma'il was wearing a white shirt, and he said to him: "O father, I have no garment in which you can shroud me other than this, so take it off so that you can shroud me in it." Abraham turned and behold, there was a white, large-eyed ram, and he slaughtered it. Ibn Abbas said: "We used to follow this type of ram."

* *

And His saying ﴿And We called to him, "O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision"﴾

This is the answer to His saying ﴿So when they had both submitted﴾, and the meaning of the speech is: "So when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead, and We called to him, 'O Abraham.'" The conjunction "wa" (and) has been inserted here, just as it was inserted in His saying ﴿until, when they came to it and its gates were opened﴾. The Arabs do this, inserting "wa" in the answer to fa-lamma (then when), and they place wa, hatta and idha before it.

By His saying ﴿you have fulfilled the vision﴾ He means the vision that We showed you in your sleep, in which We commanded you to slaughter your son.

* *

And His saying ﴿Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good﴾

He says: Just as We rewarded you for your obedience to Us, O Abraham, so We reward those who do good, who obey Our command, and who act for Our pleasure.

* *

And His saying ﴿Indeed, this was the clear trial﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed, Our command to you, O Abraham, to slaughter your son Ishaq, was truly the trial, meaning: it was the test which makes clear to whoever reflects upon it that it is a severe affliction and a great ordeal. Ibn Zayd used to say: "Trial (bala') in this context means evil, and not a test."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, this was the clear trial﴾, said: This is in the affliction which befell him, in that he was to slaughter his son. ﴿You have fulfilled the vision﴾: you were tested with a great affliction, in that you were commanded to slaughter your son. He said: This is from the disliked affliction, which is evil, and not from the trial of testing.

**Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice (107). And We left for him [a good name] among later generations (108). Peace be upon Ibrahim (109). Thus do We reward the doers of good (110). Indeed, he was among Our believing servants (111).﴾**

His words ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾ mean: We ransomed Ishaq with a great sacrifice. The fidyah (ransom) is the recompense. He says: We rewarded him by placing a great ram in the place of his slaughter, and We rescued him from being slaughtered.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) differed about which of Ibrahim's two sons was the one ransomed from slaughter. Some of them said: it was Ishaq.

Those who said this include:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, concerning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, that he said: "It was Ishaq."
- al-Husayn ibn Yazid ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The one whom Ibrahim was commanded to slaughter was Ishaq."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, that he said: "It was Ishaq."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "The one sacrificed (dhabih) was Ishaq."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Habbab narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in a narration he mentioned, that he said: "It was Ishaq."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: A man boasted in the presence of Ibn Mas'ud, saying: "I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so, son of the noble elders." Abdullah said: "That is Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the Friend of Allah."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, from al-Zuhri, from al-Ala' ibn Haritha al-Thaqafi, from Abu Hurayrah, from Ka'b, concerning His words ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, that he said: "[It was] from his son Ishaq."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya and Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Masruq, concerning His words ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, that he said: "It was Ishaq."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: "It was Ishaq."
- Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abdullah ibn Umayr, who said: (Musa said: "O Lord, they say: 'O God of Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub.' Why did they say that?" He said: "Ibrahim never placed anything equal to Me except that he chose Me over it, and Ishaq gave Himself freely for the sacrifice, while He is more generous than that, and Ya'qub, whenever I increased him in trials, increased his good opinion of Me.")
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, from his father, who said: Musa said: "O Lord, with what did You give Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub what You gave them?" Then he mentioned the meaning of the narration of Amr ibn Ali.
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan al-Shaybani, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, who said: "The sacrificed one is Ishaq."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed us, from Ibn Shihab, that Amr ibn Abi Sufyan ibn Usayd ibn Haritha al-Thaqafi informed him that Ka'b said to Abu Hurayrah: "Shall I not tell you about Ishaq, son of Ibrahim the Prophet?" Abu Hurayrah said: "Yes." Ka'b said: "When Ibrahim saw that he was going to slaughter Ishaq, Satan said: 'By Allah, if I do not tempt the family of Ibrahim at this moment, I will never tempt anyone of them ever.' So Satan took the form of a man they knew and came until, when Ibrahim went out with Ishaq to slaughter him, he entered upon Sarah, the wife of Ibrahim, and said to her: 'Where did Ibrahim go out in the morning, taking Ishaq?' Sarah said: 'He went out for some of his needs.' Satan said: 'No, by Allah, he did not go out with him for that.' Sarah said: 'Then why did he go out with him?' He said: 'He went out with him to slaughter him!' Sarah said: 'There is nothing of that; he would not slaughter his son!' Satan said: 'Yes, by Allah!' Sarah said: 'Then why would he slaughter him?' He said: 'He claims that his Lord commanded him to do so.' Sarah said: 'This is better: that he obeys his Lord, if He commanded him to do so.' So Satan left Sarah's presence and caught up with Ishaq as he walked behind his father, and said: 'Where did your father go out in the morning, taking you?' He said: 'He took me out for some of his needs.' Satan said: 'No, by Allah, he did not take you out for some of his needs, but he took you out to slaughter you.' Ishaq said: 'My father would not slaughter me!' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Why?' He said: 'He claims that his Lord commanded him to do so.' Ishaq said: 'By Allah, if his Lord commanded him to do so, he will certainly obey Him.' So Satan left him and hurried to Ibrahim and said: 'Where did you go out in the morning, taking your son?' He said: 'I went out with him for some of my needs.' He said: 'No, by Allah, you went out with him only to slaughter him.' He said: 'Why would I slaughter him?' He said: 'You claimed that your Lord commanded you to do so.' He said: 'By Allah, if my Lord commanded me to do so, I will certainly do it.' So when Ibrahim took Ishaq to slaughter him and Ishaq submitted, Allah relieved him and ransomed him with a great sacrifice. Ibrahim said to Ishaq: 'Rise, my son, for Allah has relieved you.' Allah revealed to Ishaq: 'I have given you a supplication, and I will answer you in it.' Ishaq said: 'O Allah, I ask You to answer me: whoever of the first and last [generations] meets You without associating anything with You, admit him into Paradise.'"
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, from Abu Sufyan ibn al-Ala' ibn Haritha al-Thaqafi, ally of the Banu Zuhrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from Ka'b al-Ahbar, that the one whom Ibrahim was commanded to slaughter from his two sons was Ishaq, and that when Allah relieved him and his son of the great trial they had been in, Allah said to Ishaq: "Because of your patience in obeying My command, I have given you a supplication, in which I will give you what you ask, so ask Me." He said: "My Lord, I ask You not to punish any of Your servants who meets You while believing in You." That was the request that he asked.
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Jabir, from Ibn Sabit, who said: "It was Ishaq."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uqbah narrated to us, from Hamzah al-Zayyat, from Abu Maysarah, who said: Yusuf said to the king to his face: "Would you like to eat with me? I am, by Allah, Yusuf ibn Ya'qub, the Prophet of Allah, son of Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the Friend of Allah."
- He said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, who said: Yusuf said to the king, and he mentioned something similar.

Others said: the one ransomed with the great sacrifice from the sons of Ibrahim was Isma'il.

Those who said this include:

- Abu Kurayb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib ibn al-Shahid narrated to us, both saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Thawr, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, who said: "The sacrificed one is Isma'il."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Bayan narrated to me, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, who said: "Isma'il."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamzah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Maymun al-Sukkari, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The one whom Ibrahim was commanded to slaughter was Isma'il."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Ammar, client of the Banu Hashim, or from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "It was Isma'il," meaning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾.
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "It was Isma'il."
- And Ya'qub narrated it to me again, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind was asked: "Which of Ibrahim's two sons was the one he was commanded to slaughter?" He claimed that al-Sha'bi said: Ibn Abbas said: "It was Isma'il."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Bayan, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Abbas, that he said concerning the one Allah ransomed with a great sacrifice: "It was Isma'il."
- Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Layth narrated to us, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his words ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, that he said: "It was Isma'il."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Umar ibn Qays informed me, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, that he said: "The ransomed one is Isma'il, and the Jews claimed that it was Ishaq, and the Jews lied."
- Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Mubarak, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas: "The one Allah ransomed is Isma'il."
- Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Hammad narrated to us, from Abu Asim al-Ghanawi, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.
- Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to me, saying: Khalid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Amir, who said: "The one Ibrahim intended to slaughter was Isma'il."
- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, that he said concerning this verse ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾: "It was Isma'il," and he said: "The two horns of the ram were hanging in the Ka'bah."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "The sacrificed one is Isma'il."
- He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "I saw the two horns of the ram in the Ka'bah."
- He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Mubarak ibn Fadalah, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, who said: "It was Isma'il."
- He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "It was Isma'il."
- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, concerning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, who said: "It was Isma'il."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: "I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi saying: 'The one whom Allah commanded Ibrahim to slaughter from among his sons was Isma'il. We find that in the Book of Allah, in the account of the report about Ibrahim and what he was commanded concerning the slaughter of his son Isma'il. Allah says, when He finished the story of the one to be slaughtered from Ibrahim: ﴿And We gave him the good news of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous﴾ [37:112]. That is: We gave him the good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub, meaning: a son and a son's son. He would not have commanded him to slaughter Ishaq when Ishaq had in him the promise that Allah had promised. The one whom He commanded to be slaughtered was only Isma'il.'"
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar and Amr ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan al-Basri, that he had no doubt that the one commanded to be slaughtered from the two sons of Ibrahim was Isma'il.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say that many times."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Buraydah ibn Sufyan ibn Farwah al-Aslami, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that he told them that he mentioned that to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, while he was caliph and he was with him in Syria. Umar said to him: "This is a matter I had never considered, and I see it as it is." Then he sent for a man who was with him in Syria, who had been a Jew and had embraced Islam and whose Islam was good, and who had regarded himself as one of the scholars of the Jews. Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz asked him about that. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said, while I was with Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: Umar said to him: "Which of Ibrahim's two sons was he commanded to slaughter?" He said: "Isma'il, by Allah, O Commander of the Faithful. The Jews know that, but they envy you, O Arabs, that your father should be the one concerning whom Allah's command was given and the virtue He mentioned for his patience in what he was commanded. So they deny that and claim it was Ishaq, because Ishaq is their father. Allah knows which of them it was. Each of them was pure, good, and obedient to his Lord."
- Muhammad ibn Ammar al-Razi narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Ubayd ibn Abi Karimah narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Khattabi narrated to us, from Ubayd ibn Muhammad al-Utbi, of the descendants of Utbah ibn Abi Sufyan, from his father, who said: Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated to me, from al-Sunabihi, who said: "We were with Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and they mentioned the sacrificed one, whether it was Isma'il or Ishaq. He said: 'You have stumbled upon one who knows. We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when a man came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, count for me what Allah has given you as spoils, O son of the two sacrificed ones." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed, peace and blessings be upon him. We said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, who are the two sacrificed ones?" He said: "When Abd al-Muttalib was commanded to dig Zamzam, he vowed to Allah that if its matter became easy for him, he would surely sacrifice one of his sons. The arrow fell upon Abdullah, but his maternal uncles prevented him and said: 'Ransom your son with a hundred camels,' and he ransomed him with a hundred camels. And Isma'il is the second.'"
- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, who said: "The one ransomed with it was Isma'il, and He, may His remembrance be exalted, means the ram with which Ishaq was ransomed. The Arabs say of everything prepared for slaughter: 'dhibh' (the sacrificial animal). As for dhabh with a fatha on the dhal, it is the act [of slaughtering]."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The more correct of the two views concerning the one ransomed from the two sons of Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, according to the apparent meaning of the revelation, is the view of the one who said it was Ishaq, because Allah said: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, and mentioned that He ransomed the forbearing boy whom Ibrahim was given the good news of when he asked Him to grant him a righteous son, saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a son] from among the righteous﴾ [37:100]. Then, since the one ransomed by sacrifice from his two sons was the one given the good news of, and Allah, blessed is His name, had made clear in His Book that the one given the good news of was Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub, He, may He be praised, said: ﴿So We gave her good news of Ishaq and, after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [11:71]. And in every place of the Qur'an where mention is made of His giving him the good news of a son, it is referring to Ishaq. It was clear that His giving him the good news of the forbearing boy in this place, as in His other reports in other verses of the Qur'an, is the same: [it refers to Ishaq], since it is clear that the one ransomed was the one given the good news of.

Furthermore, Allah, may His praise be exalted, informed in this verse about His Friend that He gave him the good news of the forbearing boy in response to his request that He grant him [a son] from the righteous, and it is known that he did not ask for that except when he had no child from the righteous, for he had no son from his two sons except the leader of the righteous, and [it is clear that] he did not imply that he had asked his Lord for the gift of something He had already given him. Since that is so, it is known that the one mentioned in this place, which Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, mentioned elsewhere in the Qur'an as the one given the good news of, is undoubtedly Ishaq, since the one ransomed was the one given the good news of.

As for the argument of those who argued that it was Isma'il, namely that Allah had promised Ibrahim that he would have from Ishaq a son's son, it would not have been permissible for Him to command him to slaughter [Ishaq] in light of the promise already made. Allah only commanded him to slaughter [his son] after [the son] had reached the age of striving with him, and that is a state in which it is not possible that Ishaq had children, so how could [he have had] one? As for the argument of those who argued that Allah followed the story of the one ransomed from Ibrahim's sons with His words ﴿And We gave him the good news of Ishaq, a prophet﴾ [37:112], and that if the one ransomed had been Ishaq, he would not yet have been given the good news of him, since he had already been born and had reached the age of striving with him: the good news of Ishaq's prophethood from Allah, as the reports have it, came to Ibrahim and Ishaq after he had been ransomed, as an honour from Allah to him for his patience in obeying his Lord regarding what He tested him with, namely the slaughter. The narration of those who said this has already been mentioned earlier. As for the argument of those who argued that the ram's horn was hanging in the Ka'bah, it is not impossible that it was carried from Syria to the Ka'bah. It has been narrated from a group of the people of knowledge that Ibrahim was commanded to slaughter his son Ishaq only in Syria, and that was where he intended to slaughter him.

The people of knowledge differed about the sacrifice by which Ishaq was ransomed. Some of them said: it was a ram.

Those who said this include:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Ali, concerning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, who said: "A white ram, with curved horns, and beautiful eyes, tied to a samurah tree at Thabir."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 107–111 (part 2 of 2):

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "A ram." ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: It was slaughtered at al-Maqam. Mujahid said: It was slaughtered at Mina, at the place of sacrifice (al-manhar).

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Saʿid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The ram that Ibrahim slaughtered is the ram that a son of Adam offered, and it was accepted from him.

• Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Sayyar informed us, from ʿIkrimah, that Ibn ʿAbbas had issued a ruling to one who had vowed to sacrifice himself, instructing him to sacrifice one hundred camels. He said: Ibn ʿAbbas later said: "Had I ruled for him with a ram, it would have sufficed him to slaughter a ram, for God said in His Book: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾."

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding his saying ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "It was the slaughter of a ram."

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: He turned around and there was a ram, so he took it and slaughtered it.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: The ram that Ibrahim slaughtered had grazed in Paradise for forty years, and it was a white ram with black-speckled (amlah) fleece, its wool like red woolen tufts (ʿihn).

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "With a ram."

• Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: Layth informed us, saying: Mujahid said: "The great sacrifice: a sheep."

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: and Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying ﴿with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "With a ram."
And al-Harith narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "The slaughter (al-dhibh) is the ram."

• Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: He (i.e., Ibrahim) turned around, and there was a ram; so he took it and released his son.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "The great sacrifice: the ram with which God ransomed Isaac."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from Qatadah ibn Di'amah, from Jaʿfar ibn Iyas, from ʿAbdullah ibn al-ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "A ram came forth to him from Paradise, which had grazed there for forty autumns before that. Ibrahim sent his son and followed the ram, and it took him to the first jamrah, where he struck it with seven pebbles, and then it escaped from him. It came to the middle jamrah, and he brought it out there, and struck it with seven pebbles, then it escaped him. He caught up with it at the greatest jamrah, struck it with seven pebbles, brought it out there, then took it and brought it to the place of sacrifice in Mina, and slaughtered it. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Ibn ʿAbbas, it was the beginning of Islam, and the head of the ram was hanging by its horns at the spout of the Kaʿbah, having become dried out (ḥušša), meaning dried up."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq said: "The People of the Former Scripture and many scholars claim that the sacrifice with which Ibrahim ransomed his son was a white ram, with curved horns and large eyes."

• ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Muawiyah narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "With a ram."

Others said: The sacrifice was a wild goat (waʿl).

Mention of those who said that:

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "It was a waʿl."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan, that he used to say: Ismaʿil was ransomed only with a male goat (tays) of the wild sheep (al-arwiy), which descended upon him from Thabir.

The interpreters differed regarding the reason why the sacrifice with which Isaac was ransomed was called "great." Some said: It was so called because it had grazed in Paradise.

Mention of those who said that:

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿIsa, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "It had grazed in Paradise for forty autumns."

Others said: It was called "great" because it was an accepted sacrifice (dhibhan mutaqabbalan).

Mention of those who said that:

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿great﴾, he said: "Accepted."

• al-Harith narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "The great: the accepted."

Others said: It was called "great" because it was a sacrifice slaughtered in truth, and that was his slaughter according to the religion of Ibrahim.

Mention of those who said that:

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan, that he used to say: "What God says, ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, does not refer only to his sacrifice that was slaughtered, but to slaughter in accordance with his religion; that is the sunnah until the Day of Resurrection. Know that sacrifice averts a bad death, so sacrifice, servants of God."

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: There is no statement on this more correct than what God, the Mighty and Majestic, said, namely that it should be said: God ransomed him with a great sacrifice, because God described it generally as "great" without restricting it, so it is as He described it in general terms.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾:
He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We preserved for him, among those who came after him until the Day of Resurrection, a good commendation.
As:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾, he said: God preserved for him a good commendation among the later generations.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾: Ibrahim asked, saying: ﴿And make for me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations﴾; so God left for him a good commendation among the later generations, just as He left an evil tongue upon Pharaoh and his like, so He left a truthful tongue and a righteous commendation upon these.

It was also said: The meaning of that is: And We left for him among the later generations peace, which is His saying ﴿Peace upon Ibrahim﴾. This is a statement reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: "We left his mention, because in its chain there is one whom we do not consider it proper to mention." We have already mentioned the reports concerning His saying ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾ earlier. It was also said:
The meaning is: And We left for him among the later generations that it be said: Peace upon Ibrahim.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Peace upon Ibrahim﴾:
He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: a security from God on earth for Ibrahim, that after him he be mentioned only with honorable mention.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Thus do We reward the doers of good﴾:
He says: Just as We rewarded Ibrahim for his obedience to Us and his goodness in submitting to Our command, so do We reward the good-doers. ﴿Indeed, he was among Our believing servants﴾: He says: Indeed Ibrahim was among Our servants who sincerely held faith for Us.

**Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice (107). And We left for him [a good name] among later generations (108). Peace be upon Ibrahim (109). Thus do We reward the doers of good (110). Indeed, he was among Our believing servants (111).﴾**

His words ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾ mean: We ransomed Ishaq with a great sacrifice. The fidyah (ransom) is the recompense. He says: We rewarded him by placing a great ram in the place of his slaughter, and We rescued him from being slaughtered.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) differed about which of Ibrahim's two sons was the one ransomed from slaughter. Some of them said: it was Ishaq.

Those who said this include:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, concerning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, that he said: "It was Ishaq."
- al-Husayn ibn Yazid ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The one whom Ibrahim was commanded to slaughter was Ishaq."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, that he said: "It was Ishaq."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "The one sacrificed (dhabih) was Ishaq."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Habbab narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in a narration he mentioned, that he said: "It was Ishaq."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: A man boasted in the presence of Ibn Mas'ud, saying: "I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so, son of the noble elders." Abdullah said: "That is Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the Friend of Allah."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, from al-Zuhri, from al-Ala' ibn Haritha al-Thaqafi, from Abu Hurayrah, from Ka'b, concerning His words ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, that he said: "[It was] from his son Ishaq."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya and Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Masruq, concerning His words ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, that he said: "It was Ishaq."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: "It was Ishaq."
- Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abdullah ibn Umayr, who said: (Musa said: "O Lord, they say: 'O God of Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub.' Why did they say that?" He said: "Ibrahim never placed anything equal to Me except that he chose Me over it, and Ishaq gave Himself freely for the sacrifice, while He is more generous than that, and Ya'qub, whenever I increased him in trials, increased his good opinion of Me.")
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, from his father, who said: Musa said: "O Lord, with what did You give Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub what You gave them?" Then he mentioned the meaning of the narration of Amr ibn Ali.
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan al-Shaybani, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, who said: "The sacrificed one is Ishaq."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed us, from Ibn Shihab, that Amr ibn Abi Sufyan ibn Usayd ibn Haritha al-Thaqafi informed him that Ka'b said to Abu Hurayrah: "Shall I not tell you about Ishaq, son of Ibrahim the Prophet?" Abu Hurayrah said: "Yes." Ka'b said: "When Ibrahim saw that he was going to slaughter Ishaq, Satan said: 'By Allah, if I do not tempt the family of Ibrahim at this moment, I will never tempt anyone of them ever.' So Satan took the form of a man they knew and came until, when Ibrahim went out with Ishaq to slaughter him, he entered upon Sarah, the wife of Ibrahim, and said to her: 'Where did Ibrahim go out in the morning, taking Ishaq?' Sarah said: 'He went out for some of his needs.' Satan said: 'No, by Allah, he did not go out with him for that.' Sarah said: 'Then why did he go out with him?' He said: 'He went out with him to slaughter him!' Sarah said: 'There is nothing of that; he would not slaughter his son!' Satan said: 'Yes, by Allah!' Sarah said: 'Then why would he slaughter him?' He said: 'He claims that his Lord commanded him to do so.' Sarah said: 'This is better: that he obeys his Lord, if He commanded him to do so.' So Satan left Sarah's presence and caught up with Ishaq as he walked behind his father, and said: 'Where did your father go out in the morning, taking you?' He said: 'He took me out for some of his needs.' Satan said: 'No, by Allah, he did not take you out for some of his needs, but he took you out to slaughter you.' Ishaq said: 'My father would not slaughter me!' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Why?' He said: 'He claims that his Lord commanded him to do so.' Ishaq said: 'By Allah, if his Lord commanded him to do so, he will certainly obey Him.' So Satan left him and hurried to Ibrahim and said: 'Where did you go out in the morning, taking your son?' He said: 'I went out with him for some of my needs.' He said: 'No, by Allah, you went out with him only to slaughter him.' He said: 'Why would I slaughter him?' He said: 'You claimed that your Lord commanded you to do so.' He said: 'By Allah, if my Lord commanded me to do so, I will certainly do it.' So when Ibrahim took Ishaq to slaughter him and Ishaq submitted, Allah relieved him and ransomed him with a great sacrifice. Ibrahim said to Ishaq: 'Rise, my son, for Allah has relieved you.' Allah revealed to Ishaq: 'I have given you a supplication, and I will answer you in it.' Ishaq said: 'O Allah, I ask You to answer me: whoever of the first and last [generations] meets You without associating anything with You, admit him into Paradise.'"
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, from Abu Sufyan ibn al-Ala' ibn Haritha al-Thaqafi, ally of the Banu Zuhrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from Ka'b al-Ahbar, that the one whom Ibrahim was commanded to slaughter from his two sons was Ishaq, and that when Allah relieved him and his son of the great trial they had been in, Allah said to Ishaq: "Because of your patience in obeying My command, I have given you a supplication, in which I will give you what you ask, so ask Me." He said: "My Lord, I ask You not to punish any of Your servants who meets You while believing in You." That was the request that he asked.
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Jabir, from Ibn Sabit, who said: "It was Ishaq."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uqbah narrated to us, from Hamzah al-Zayyat, from Abu Maysarah, who said: Yusuf said to the king to his face: "Would you like to eat with me? I am, by Allah, Yusuf ibn Ya'qub, the Prophet of Allah, son of Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the Friend of Allah."
- He said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, who said: Yusuf said to the king, and he mentioned something similar.

Others said: the one ransomed with the great sacrifice from the sons of Ibrahim was Isma'il.

Those who said this include:

- Abu Kurayb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib ibn al-Shahid narrated to us, both saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Thawr, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, who said: "The sacrificed one is Isma'il."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Bayan narrated to me, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, who said: "Isma'il."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamzah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Maymun al-Sukkari, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The one whom Ibrahim was commanded to slaughter was Isma'il."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Ammar, client of the Banu Hashim, or from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "It was Isma'il," meaning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾.
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "It was Isma'il."
- And Ya'qub narrated it to me again, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind was asked: "Which of Ibrahim's two sons was the one he was commanded to slaughter?" He claimed that al-Sha'bi said: Ibn Abbas said: "It was Isma'il."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Bayan, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Abbas, that he said concerning the one Allah ransomed with a great sacrifice: "It was Isma'il."
- Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Layth narrated to us, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his words ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, that he said: "It was Isma'il."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Umar ibn Qays informed me, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, that he said: "The ransomed one is Isma'il, and the Jews claimed that it was Ishaq, and the Jews lied."
- Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Mubarak, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas: "The one Allah ransomed is Isma'il."
- Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Hammad narrated to us, from Abu Asim al-Ghanawi, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.
- Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to me, saying: Khalid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Amir, who said: "The one Ibrahim intended to slaughter was Isma'il."
- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, that he said concerning this verse ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾: "It was Isma'il," and he said: "The two horns of the ram were hanging in the Ka'bah."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "The sacrificed one is Isma'il."
- He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "I saw the two horns of the ram in the Ka'bah."
- He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Mubarak ibn Fadalah, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, who said: "It was Isma'il."
- He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "It was Isma'il."
- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, concerning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, who said: "It was Isma'il."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: "I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi saying: 'The one whom Allah commanded Ibrahim to slaughter from among his sons was Isma'il. We find that in the Book of Allah, in the account of the report about Ibrahim and what he was commanded concerning the slaughter of his son Isma'il. Allah says, when He finished the story of the one to be slaughtered from Ibrahim: ﴿And We gave him the good news of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous﴾ [37:112]. That is: We gave him the good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub, meaning: a son and a son's son. He would not have commanded him to slaughter Ishaq when Ishaq had in him the promise that Allah had promised. The one whom He commanded to be slaughtered was only Isma'il.'"
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar and Amr ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan al-Basri, that he had no doubt that the one commanded to be slaughtered from the two sons of Ibrahim was Isma'il.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say that many times."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Buraydah ibn Sufyan ibn Farwah al-Aslami, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that he told them that he mentioned that to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, while he was caliph and he was with him in Syria. Umar said to him: "This is a matter I had never considered, and I see it as it is." Then he sent for a man who was with him in Syria, who had been a Jew and had embraced Islam and whose Islam was good, and who had regarded himself as one of the scholars of the Jews. Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz asked him about that. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said, while I was with Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: Umar said to him: "Which of Ibrahim's two sons was he commanded to slaughter?" He said: "Isma'il, by Allah, O Commander of the Faithful. The Jews know that, but they envy you, O Arabs, that your father should be the one concerning whom Allah's command was given and the virtue He mentioned for his patience in what he was commanded. So they deny that and claim it was Ishaq, because Ishaq is their father. Allah knows which of them it was. Each of them was pure, good, and obedient to his Lord."
- Muhammad ibn Ammar al-Razi narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Ubayd ibn Abi Karimah narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Khattabi narrated to us, from Ubayd ibn Muhammad al-Utbi, of the descendants of Utbah ibn Abi Sufyan, from his father, who said: Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated to me, from al-Sunabihi, who said: "We were with Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and they mentioned the sacrificed one, whether it was Isma'il or Ishaq. He said: 'You have stumbled upon one who knows. We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when a man came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, count for me what Allah has given you as spoils, O son of the two sacrificed ones." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed, peace and blessings be upon him. We said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, who are the two sacrificed ones?" He said: "When Abd al-Muttalib was commanded to dig Zamzam, he vowed to Allah that if its matter became easy for him, he would surely sacrifice one of his sons. The arrow fell upon Abdullah, but his maternal uncles prevented him and said: 'Ransom your son with a hundred camels,' and he ransomed him with a hundred camels. And Isma'il is the second.'"
- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, who said: "The one ransomed with it was Isma'il, and He, may His remembrance be exalted, means the ram with which Ishaq was ransomed. The Arabs say of everything prepared for slaughter: 'dhibh' (the sacrificial animal). As for dhabh with a fatha on the dhal, it is the act [of slaughtering]."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The more correct of the two views concerning the one ransomed from the two sons of Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, according to the apparent meaning of the revelation, is the view of the one who said it was Ishaq, because Allah said: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, and mentioned that He ransomed the forbearing boy whom Ibrahim was given the good news of when he asked Him to grant him a righteous son, saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a son] from among the righteous﴾ [37:100]. Then, since the one ransomed by sacrifice from his two sons was the one given the good news of, and Allah, blessed is His name, had made clear in His Book that the one given the good news of was Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub, He, may He be praised, said: ﴿So We gave her good news of Ishaq and, after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [11:71]. And in every place of the Qur'an where mention is made of His giving him the good news of a son, it is referring to Ishaq. It was clear that His giving him the good news of the forbearing boy in this place, as in His other reports in other verses of the Qur'an, is the same: [it refers to Ishaq], since it is clear that the one ransomed was the one given the good news of.

Furthermore, Allah, may His praise be exalted, informed in this verse about His Friend that He gave him the good news of the forbearing boy in response to his request that He grant him [a son] from the righteous, and it is known that he did not ask for that except when he had no child from the righteous, for he had no son from his two sons except the leader of the righteous, and [it is clear that] he did not imply that he had asked his Lord for the gift of something He had already given him. Since that is so, it is known that the one mentioned in this place, which Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, mentioned elsewhere in the Qur'an as the one given the good news of, is undoubtedly Ishaq, since the one ransomed was the one given the good news of.

As for the argument of those who argued that it was Isma'il, namely that Allah had promised Ibrahim that he would have from Ishaq a son's son, it would not have been permissible for Him to command him to slaughter [Ishaq] in light of the promise already made. Allah only commanded him to slaughter [his son] after [the son] had reached the age of striving with him, and that is a state in which it is not possible that Ishaq had children, so how could [he have had] one? As for the argument of those who argued that Allah followed the story of the one ransomed from Ibrahim's sons with His words ﴿And We gave him the good news of Ishaq, a prophet﴾ [37:112], and that if the one ransomed had been Ishaq, he would not yet have been given the good news of him, since he had already been born and had reached the age of striving with him: the good news of Ishaq's prophethood from Allah, as the reports have it, came to Ibrahim and Ishaq after he had been ransomed, as an honour from Allah to him for his patience in obeying his Lord regarding what He tested him with, namely the slaughter. The narration of those who said this has already been mentioned earlier. As for the argument of those who argued that the ram's horn was hanging in the Ka'bah, it is not impossible that it was carried from Syria to the Ka'bah. It has been narrated from a group of the people of knowledge that Ibrahim was commanded to slaughter his son Ishaq only in Syria, and that was where he intended to slaughter him.

The people of knowledge differed about the sacrifice by which Ishaq was ransomed. Some of them said: it was a ram.

Those who said this include:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Ali, concerning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, who said: "A white ram, with curved horns, and beautiful eyes, tied to a samurah tree at Thabir."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 107–111 (part 2 of 2):

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "A ram." ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: It was slaughtered at al-Maqam. Mujahid said: It was slaughtered at Mina, at the place of sacrifice (al-manhar).

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Saʿid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The ram that Ibrahim slaughtered is the ram that a son of Adam offered, and it was accepted from him.

• Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Sayyar informed us, from ʿIkrimah, that Ibn ʿAbbas had issued a ruling to one who had vowed to sacrifice himself, instructing him to sacrifice one hundred camels. He said: Ibn ʿAbbas later said: "Had I ruled for him with a ram, it would have sufficed him to slaughter a ram, for God said in His Book: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾."

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding his saying ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "It was the slaughter of a ram."
