The arrow fell upon Abdullah, but his maternal uncles prevented him and said: 'Ransom your son with a hundred camels,' and he ransomed him with a hundred camels. And Isma'il is the second.'"
- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, who said: "The one ransomed with it was Isma'il, and He, may His remembrance be exalted, means the ram with which Ishaq was ransomed. The Arabs say of everything prepared for slaughter: 'dhibh' (the sacrificial animal). As for dhabh with a fatha on the dhal, it is the act [of slaughtering]."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The more correct of the two views concerning the one ransomed from the two sons of Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, according to the apparent meaning of the revelation, is the view of the one who said it was Ishaq, because Allah said: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, and mentioned that He ransomed the forbearing boy whom Ibrahim was given the good news of when he asked Him to grant him a righteous son, saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a son] from among the righteous﴾ [37:100]. Then, since the one ransomed by sacrifice from his two sons was the one given the good news of, and Allah, blessed is His name, had made clear in His Book that the one given the good news of was Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub, He, may He be praised, said: ﴿So We gave her good news of Ishaq and, after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [11:71]. And in every place of the Qur'an where mention is made of His giving him the good news of a son, it is referring to Ishaq. It was clear that His giving him the good news of the forbearing boy in this place, as in His other reports in other verses of the Qur'an, is the same: [it refers to Ishaq], since it is clear that the one ransomed was the one given the good news of.

Furthermore, Allah, may His praise be exalted, informed in this verse about His Friend that He gave him the good news of the forbearing boy in response to his request that He grant him [a son] from the righteous, and it is known that he did not ask for that except when he had no child from the righteous, for he had no son from his two sons except the leader of the righteous, and [it is clear that] he did not imply that he had asked his Lord for the gift of something He had already given him. Since that is so, it is known that the one mentioned in this place, which Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, mentioned elsewhere in the Qur'an as the one given the good news of, is undoubtedly Ishaq, since the one ransomed was the one given the good news of.

As for the argument of those who argued that it was Isma'il, namely that Allah had promised Ibrahim that he would have from Ishaq a son's son, it would not have been permissible for Him to command him to slaughter [Ishaq] in light of the promise already made. Allah only commanded him to slaughter [his son] after [the son] had reached the age of striving with him, and that is a state in which it is not possible that Ishaq had children, so how could [he have had] one? As for the argument of those who argued that Allah followed the story of the one ransomed from Ibrahim's sons with His words ﴿And We gave him the good news of Ishaq, a prophet﴾ [37:112], and that if the one ransomed had been Ishaq, he would not yet have been given the good news of him, since he had already been born and had reached the age of striving with him: the good news of Ishaq's prophethood from Allah, as the reports have it, came to Ibrahim and Ishaq after he had been ransomed, as an honour from Allah to him for his patience in obeying his Lord regarding what He tested him with, namely the slaughter. The narration of those who said this has already been mentioned earlier. As for the argument of those who argued that the ram's horn was hanging in the Ka'bah, it is not impossible that it was carried from Syria to the Ka'bah. It has been narrated from a group of the people of knowledge that Ibrahim was commanded to slaughter his son Ishaq only in Syria, and that was where he intended to slaughter him.

The people of knowledge differed about the sacrifice by which Ishaq was ransomed. Some of them said: it was a ram.

Those who said this include:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Ali, concerning ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, who said: "A white ram, with curved horns, and beautiful eyes, tied to a samurah tree at Thabir."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 107–111 (part 2 of 2):

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "A ram." ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: It was slaughtered at al-Maqam. Mujahid said: It was slaughtered at Mina, at the place of sacrifice (al-manhar).

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Saʿid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The ram that Ibrahim slaughtered is the ram that a son of Adam offered, and it was accepted from him.

• Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Sayyar informed us, from ʿIkrimah, that Ibn ʿAbbas had issued a ruling to one who had vowed to sacrifice himself, instructing him to sacrifice one hundred camels. He said: Ibn ʿAbbas later said: "Had I ruled for him with a ram, it would have sufficed him to slaughter a ram, for God said in His Book: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾."

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding his saying ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "It was the slaughter of a ram."

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: He turned around and there was a ram, so he took it and slaughtered it.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: The ram that Ibrahim slaughtered had grazed in Paradise for forty years, and it was a white ram with black-speckled (amlah) fleece, its wool like red woolen tufts (ʿihn).

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "With a ram."

• Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: Layth informed us, saying: Mujahid said: "The great sacrifice: a sheep."

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: and Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying ﴿with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "With a ram."
And al-Harith narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "The slaughter (al-dhibh) is the ram."

• Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: He (i.e., Ibrahim) turned around, and there was a ram; so he took it and released his son.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "The great sacrifice: the ram with which God ransomed Isaac."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from Qatadah ibn Di'amah, from Jaʿfar ibn Iyas, from ʿAbdullah ibn al-ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "A ram came forth to him from Paradise, which had grazed there for forty autumns before that. Ibrahim sent his son and followed the ram, and it took him to the first jamrah, where he struck it with seven pebbles, and then it escaped from him. It came to the middle jamrah, and he brought it out there, and struck it with seven pebbles, then it escaped him. He caught up with it at the greatest jamrah, struck it with seven pebbles, brought it out there, then took it and brought it to the place of sacrifice in Mina, and slaughtered it. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Ibn ʿAbbas, it was the beginning of Islam, and the head of the ram was hanging by its horns at the spout of the Kaʿbah, having become dried out (ḥušša), meaning dried up."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq said: "The People of the Former Scripture and many scholars claim that the sacrifice with which Ibrahim ransomed his son was a white ram, with curved horns and large eyes."

• ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Muawiyah narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "With a ram."

Others said: The sacrifice was a wild goat (waʿl).

Mention of those who said that:

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "It was a waʿl."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan, that he used to say: Ismaʿil was ransomed only with a male goat (tays) of the wild sheep (al-arwiy), which descended upon him from Thabir.

The interpreters differed regarding the reason why the sacrifice with which Isaac was ransomed was called "great." Some said: It was so called because it had grazed in Paradise.

Mention of those who said that:

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿIsa, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "It had grazed in Paradise for forty autumns."

Others said: It was called "great" because it was an accepted sacrifice (dhibhan mutaqabbalan).

Mention of those who said that:

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿great﴾, he said: "Accepted."

• al-Harith narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, he said: "The great: the accepted."

Others said: It was called "great" because it was a sacrifice slaughtered in truth, and that was his slaughter according to the religion of Ibrahim.

Mention of those who said that:

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan, that he used to say: "What God says, ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, does not refer only to his sacrifice that was slaughtered, but to slaughter in accordance with his religion; that is the sunnah until the Day of Resurrection. Know that sacrifice averts a bad death, so sacrifice, servants of God."

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: There is no statement on this more correct than what God, the Mighty and Majestic, said, namely that it should be said: God ransomed him with a great sacrifice, because God described it generally as "great" without restricting it, so it is as He described it in general terms.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾:
He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We preserved for him, among those who came after him until the Day of Resurrection, a good commendation.
As:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾, he said: God preserved for him a good commendation among the later generations.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾: Ibrahim asked, saying: ﴿And make for me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations﴾; so God left for him a good commendation among the later generations, just as He left an evil tongue upon Pharaoh and his like, so He left a truthful tongue and a righteous commendation upon these.

It was also said: The meaning of that is: And We left for him among the later generations peace, which is His saying ﴿Peace upon Ibrahim﴾. This is a statement reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: "We left his mention, because in its chain there is one whom we do not consider it proper to mention." We have already mentioned the reports concerning His saying ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾ earlier. It was also said:
The meaning is: And We left for him among the later generations that it be said: Peace upon Ibrahim.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Peace upon Ibrahim﴾:
He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: a security from God on earth for Ibrahim, that after him he be mentioned only with honorable mention.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Thus do We reward the doers of good﴾:
He says: Just as We rewarded Ibrahim for his obedience to Us and his goodness in submitting to Our command, so do We reward the good-doers. ﴿Indeed, he was among Our believing servants﴾: He says: Indeed Ibrahim was among Our servants who sincerely held faith for Us.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 112–113:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous (112). And We blessed him and Isaac. And among their descendants are the good-doers and those who clearly wrong themselves (113).﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: And We gave Abraham good tidings of Isaac, a prophet, in thanks for his good deeds and obedience.

As follows:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous﴾, he said: He was given good tidings of him as a prophet after that, after this matter of his had occurred when he surrendered himself to Allah.

* Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: The one who was sacrificed was Isaac. He said: And His saying, ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous﴾, he said: He was given good tidings of his prophethood. He said: And His saying, ﴿And We gave him from Our mercy his brother Aaron, a prophet﴾, he said: Aaron was older than Moses, but He willed to grant him prophethood.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard Dawud relate, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning this verse, ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous﴾, he said: He gave him the good tidings of him as a prophet only when He ransomed him from the sacrifice, and the good tidings of prophethood were not at his birth.

* Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Tahhan narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet﴾, he said: He was given good tidings of prophethood.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous﴾, he said: Abraham was given good tidings of Isaac.

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous﴾, he said: Concerning his prophethood.

* Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Dirar, from a shaykh from the people of the mosque, who said: Abraham was given good tidings of Isaac when he was one hundred and seventeen years old.

* * *

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: And We blessed Abraham and Isaac. ﴿And among their descendants are the good-doers﴾, meaning by the good-doer: the believer who obeys Allah, who is good in his obedience to Him. ﴿And those who clearly wrong themselves﴾, and meaning by one who wrongs himself: the disbeliever in Allah, who brings upon himself, by his disbelief, the punishment of Allah and the painfulness of His retribution. ﴿Clearly (mubin)﴾: meaning one who has made manifest his wronging of himself through his disbelief in Allah.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying, ﴿good-doer and those who clearly wrong themselves﴾, he said: The good-doer is the one who obeys Allah, and the one who wrongs himself is the one who disobeys Allah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verses 114–116:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We bestowed Our favour upon Moses and Aaron. And We saved them and their people from the great distress. And We helped them, so they were the victors.﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: We showed grace to Moses and Aaron, the two sons of ʿImran, so We made them both prophets, and We saved them and their people from the grief and great hardship they were in, namely the servitude of the people of Pharaoh, and from what We destroyed Pharaoh and his people with, namely drowning.

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said on this point.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words ﴿and We saved them and their people from the great distress﴾, he said: from drowning.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿and We saved them and their people from the great distress﴾: that is, from the people of Pharaoh.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿And We helped them﴾:

He means: We helped Moses, Aaron and their people against Pharaoh and his household by drowning them, ﴿so they were the victors﴾ over them.

Some scholars of Arabic grammar (ahl al-ʿArabiyya) said: the pronoun in His words ﴿And We helped them﴾ (the hāʾ and mīm) is intended to refer to Moses and Aaron, but it is expressed in the form of a plural pronoun, because the Arabs refer to a leader, such as a prophet or a commander and the like, by way of his followers and soldiers, using the plural, and at other times by way of the singular, since he is one in origin. A similar usage is: ﴿out of fear of Pharaoh and their chieftains﴾, and in another place: "and his chieftain". He said: Sometimes the Arabs also refer to two persons in the plural, just as they refer to one person in the plural, so they address a man and say: "You did not do well and you were not gracious," while they mean him alone. This view which we have reported from this speaker concerning His words ﴿And We helped them﴾, although it is not rejected, is not something we need to strain to support, since God follows that with His words ﴿And We saved them and their people from the great distress﴾, and then says ﴿And We helped them﴾, meaning: they and their people, because Pharaoh and his people were enemies of all the Children of Israel, who had oppressed them, slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive, so God helped them against them by drowning them and saving the others.

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And We gave them both the Clear Book﴾ [117] ﴿and guided them to the Straight Path﴾ [118] ﴿and We left for them among later generations﴾ [119] ﴿Peace be upon Moses and Aaron﴾ [120] ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾ [121] ﴿Indeed, they were among Our believing servants﴾ [122].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We gave Moses and Aaron the Book, meaning the Torah.

As related:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We gave them both the Clear Book﴾: the Torah.

By "al-mustabin" (the clear, manifest) is meant that its guidance, its detailed explanations and its rulings are made evident.

* *

As for His words ﴿and guided them to the Straight Path﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We guided Moses and Aaron to the straight path, which has no crookedness in it, and it is Islam, the religion of God, with which He sent His prophets.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and guided them to the Straight Path﴾: Islam.

He says: And We left for them among the later generations after them a good commendation.

* *

He says: That it be said: Peace be upon Moses and Aaron.

He says: Thus do We reward the people of Our obedience and those who act in ways that please Us, ﴿Indeed, they were among Our believing servants﴾, meaning: Indeed Moses and Aaron were among Our servants who were sincere to Us in faith.

Ilyas, who is Ilyas ibn Yasin ibn Finhas ibn al-'Izar ibn Harun ibn Imran, according to what is said:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq.

* *

As for His words, ﴿among the messengers﴾:

He, may His mention be exalted, says: [He was] one of the messengers ﴿when he said to his people, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾

That is, when he said to his people among the Children of Israel: "Will you not fear Allah, O people, so that you fear Him and beware of His punishment for worshipping a lord other than Allah and a god besides Him?" ﴿And forsake the best of creators﴾ means: and you abandon the worship of the best of those who are called creators.

The meaning of Ba'l has been disputed. Some said: its meaning is "Do you call upon a lord?" and they said it is a dialect of the people of Yemen, known among them.

Those who said this:

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Harami ibn 'Umarah narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: 'Umarah informed me, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l﴾, he said: "A god."

* 'Imran ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: 'Umarah narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l﴾, he said: "Do you call upon a lord?" and it is the dialect of the people of Yemen; they say: "Whose Ba'l is this bull?" meaning: "Who is its lord?"

* Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah and Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, both saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l﴾, he said: "A lord."

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l﴾, he said: "A lord."

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: I was with Ibn 'Abbas when they asked him about this verse: ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l﴾. He said: Ibn 'Abbas fell silent, then a man said: "I am its Ba'l," and Ibn 'Abbas said: "This answer suffices me."

Others said: It is an idol they had called Ba'l, and by it Ba'labakk was named.

Those who said this:

* It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l﴾: he means an idol they had, called Ba'l.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l and forsake the best of creators?﴾: Ba'l is an idol they used to worship; they were at Ba'labakk, beyond Damascus, and the Ba'l they worshipped was there.

Others said: Ba'l was a woman whom they worshipped.

Those who said this:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: I heard some people of knowledge say: Ba'l was nothing but a woman they worshipped besides Allah.

In the speech of the Arabs, Ba'l has several meanings. They say of the owner of a thing that he is its ba'l, as it is said: "This is the ba'l of this house," meaning its owner. They say of a woman's husband that he is her ba'l. And they say of plantings and crops that are self-sufficient through rainwater, not needing irrigation, that they are ba'l, and this is al-'Adhy. It is mentioned that Allah sent Ilyas to the Children of Israel after the death of Hizqil ibn Yuzha.

As for his story and the story of his people, as it has reached us:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Allah took Hizqil, and transgressions grew great among the Children of Israel, and they forgot what covenant Allah had made with them, until they set up idols and worshipped them besides Allah. So Allah sent to them Ilyas ibn Yasin ibn Finhas ibn al-'Izar ibn Harun ibn Imran as a prophet. The prophets among the Children of Israel after Musa were sent to them only to renew what had been forgotten of the Torah. Ilyas was with a king of the kings of the Children of Israel called Ahab, whose wife was named Irbal; he listened to him and believed him, and Ilyas would manage his affairs for him. But the rest of the Children of Israel had taken an idol they worshipped besides Allah, called Ba'l.

Ibn Ishaq said: I heard some people of knowledge say: Ba'l was nothing but a woman they worshipped besides Allah; Allah says to Muhammad: ﴿And indeed, Ilyas was among the messengers. When he said to his people, "Will you not fear Allah? Do you call upon Ba'l and forsake the best of creators, Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest ones?"﴾ So Ilyas began calling them to Allah, but they would not listen to him except for that king, while the kings were scattered throughout Syria, each king having a region of it which he consumed. That king with whom Ilyas was would manage his affairs and regard him as rightly guided among his companions. One day he said: "O Ilyas, by Allah, I do not see what you call to be anything but falsehood. By Allah, I do not see that so-and-so and so-and-so," enumerating kings of the Children of Israel who had worshipped idols besides Allah, "are anything but upon the same as us: they eat, drink, and live in luxury as rulers, and what you claim is false does not diminish their worldly affairs, and we do not see any superiority of yours over them." So, it is claimed—and Allah knows best—that Ilyas said "Inna lillah" and his hair and skin stood up, then he left him and departed. That king did as his companions did: he worshipped idols and did what they did. Ilyas said: "O Allah, the Children of Israel have refused except to disbelieve in You and worship other than You; change what You have given them of Your blessing." Or as he said.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: It was mentioned to me that it was revealed to him: "We have placed the matter of their provision in your hand and under your authority, so that you are the one who permits it." Ilyas said: "O Allah, then withhold the rain from them." So He withheld it from them for three years, until the livestock, the insects, the beasts, and the trees perished, and the people suffered a severe hardship. Ilyas, it is said, when he prayed this against the Children of Israel, had gone into hiding, out of concern for himself from them. Wherever he was, provision was set for him, and when they smelled the scent of bread in a house or room, they said: "Ilyas has entered this place," and they searched for him, and the people of that house met evil from them. Then he took refuge one night with a woman of the Children of Israel who had a son called al-Yasa' ibn Akhtub, who was afflicted with harm. She sheltered him and concealed his matter, and Ilyas prayed for her son, and he was healed of the harm he had. Al-Yasa' followed Ilyas as a young man. It is claimed—and Allah knows best—that Allah revealed to Ilyas: "You have destroyed many creatures who have not disobeyed, besides the Children of Israel, of beasts, animals, birds, insects, and trees, by withholding the rain from the Children of Israel." It is claimed—and Allah knows best—that Ilyas said: "My Lord, let me be the one who prays for them, and let me be the one who brings them relief from what they are in of the trial that has befallen them, perhaps they will return and desist from what they are upon of worshipping other than You." It was said to him: "Yes." So Ilyas came to the Children of Israel and said to them: "You have perished from hunger, and the beasts, animals, birds, insects, and trees have perished because of your sins, and you are upon falsehood and delusion," or as he said to them, "If you wish to know this, and to know that Allah is angry with you for what you are upon, and that what I call you to is the truth, then go out with these idols of yours that you worship and claim are better than what I call you to. If they respond to you, then it is as you say; but if they do not act, you will know that you are upon falsehood, and you will desist, and I will pray to Allah and He will relieve you of what you are in of trial." They said: "You have been fair." So they went out with their idols, and with what they drew near to Allah with of their innovations which He does not accept, and they called upon them, but they did not respond to them, nor did they relieve them of what they were in of trial, until they recognized the misguidance and falsehood they were in. Then they said to Ilyas: "O Ilyas, we have perished, so pray to Allah for us." Ilyas prayed for them for relief from what they were in, and that they be given rain. A cloud came out like a shield by Allah's permission over the sea while they watched, then the clouds gathered toward it, then it poured, and He sent the rain, and it relieved them, their lands became green, and relief came to them from what they had been in of the trial. Yet they did not desist and did not return, and they remained upon the most wicked of what they had been upon. When Ilyas saw their disbelief, he asked his Lord to take him to Himself and relieve him of them. It was said to him, as they claim: "Look on such-and-such a day; go out on it to such-and-such a land, and whatever comes to you, mount it and do not give it away." Ilyas went out, and al-Yasa' ibn Akhtub went out with him, until when he was in the town mentioned to him, at the place he had been commanded, there came to him a horse of fire until it stood before him, and he leapt upon it and departed with it. Al-Yasa' called to him: "O Ilyas, O Ilyas, what do you command me?" That was the last of their contact with him. Allah clothed him with feathers, dressed him in light, cut off from him the pleasure of food and drink, and he flew among the angels. He was a human, angelic, earthly, and heavenly being.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest ones﴾. The majority of the readers of Mecca, Medina, and Basra, and some of the readers of Kufa, recited it: ﴿Allah, your Lord (Rabbukum) and the Lord (Rabbu) of your forefathers, the earliest ones﴾, with the nominative, as a new sentence, and that the statement ends at His words ﴿the best of creators﴾. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it: ﴿Allah, your Lord (Rabbakum) and the Lord (Raba) of your forefathers, the earliest ones﴾, with the accusative, as a response to His words ﴿and forsake the best of creators﴾, on the basis that all of it is one speech.

The correct view, in our opinion, is that these are two recitations close in meaning, and since both recitations are widely transmitted among the readers, whichever one the reader recites is correct. The meaning of the speech is: That is your object of worship, O people, which deserves worship from you: your Lord who created you, and the Lord of your forefathers who came before you, not the idol that creates nothing and neither harms nor benefits.

* It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l﴾: he means an idol they had, called Ba'l.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l and forsake the best of creators?﴾: Ba'l is an idol they used to worship; they were at Ba'labakk, beyond Damascus, and the Ba'l they worshipped was there.

Others said: Ba'l was a woman whom they worshipped.

Those who said this:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: I heard some people of knowledge say: Ba'l was nothing but a woman they worshipped besides Allah.

In the speech of the Arabs, Ba'l has several meanings. They say of the owner of a thing that he is its ba'l, as it is said: "This is the ba'l of this house," meaning its owner. They say of a woman's husband that he is her ba'l. And they say of plantings and crops that are self-sufficient through rainwater, not needing irrigation, that they are ba'l, and this is al-'Adhy. It is mentioned that Allah sent Ilyas to the Children of Israel after the death of Hizqil ibn Yuzha.

As for his story and the story of his people, as it has reached us:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Allah took Hizqil, and transgressions grew great among the Children of Israel, and they forgot what covenant Allah had made with them, until they set up idols and worshipped them besides Allah. So Allah sent to them Ilyas ibn Yasin ibn Finhas ibn al-'Izar ibn Harun ibn Imran as a prophet. The prophets among the Children of Israel after Musa were sent to them only to renew what had been forgotten of the Torah. Ilyas was with a king of the kings of the Children of Israel called Ahab, whose wife was named Irbal; he listened to him and believed him, and Ilyas would manage his affairs for him. But the rest of the Children of Israel had taken an idol they worshipped besides Allah, called Ba'l.

Ibn Ishaq said: I heard some people of knowledge say: Ba'l was nothing but a woman they worshipped besides Allah; Allah says to Muhammad: ﴿And indeed, Ilyas was among the messengers. When he said to his people, "Will you not fear Allah? Do you call upon Ba'l and forsake the best of creators, Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest ones?"﴾ So Ilyas began calling them to Allah, but they would not listen to him except for that king, while the kings were scattered throughout Syria, each king having a region of it which he consumed. That king with whom Ilyas was would manage his affairs and regard him as rightly guided among his companions. One day he said: "O Ilyas, by Allah, I do not see what you call to be anything but falsehood. By Allah, I do not see that so-and-so and so-and-so," enumerating kings of the Children of Israel who had worshipped idols besides Allah, "are anything but upon the same as us: they eat, drink, and live in luxury as rulers, and what you claim is false does not diminish their worldly affairs, and we do not see any superiority of yours over them." So, it is claimed—and Allah knows best—that Ilyas said "Inna lillah" and his hair and skin stood up, then he left him and departed. That king did as his companions did: he worshipped idols and did what they did. Ilyas said: "O Allah, the Children of Israel have refused except to disbelieve in You and worship other than You; change what You have given them of Your blessing." Or as he said.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: It was mentioned to me that it was revealed to him: "We have placed the matter of their provision in your hand and under your authority, so that you are the one who permits it." Ilyas said: "O Allah, then withhold the rain from them." So He withheld it from them for three years, until the livestock, the insects, the beasts, and the trees perished, and the people suffered a severe hardship. Ilyas, it is said, when he prayed this against the Children of Israel, had gone into hiding, out of concern for himself from them. Wherever he was, provision was set for him, and when they smelled the scent of bread in a house or room, they said: "Ilyas has entered this place," and they searched for him, and the people of that house met evil from them. Then he took refuge one night with a woman of the Children of Israel who had a son called al-Yasa' ibn Akhtub, who was afflicted with harm. She sheltered him and concealed his matter, and Ilyas prayed for her son, and he was healed of the harm he had. Al-Yasa' followed Ilyas as a young man. It is claimed—and Allah knows best—that Allah revealed to Ilyas: "You have destroyed many creatures who have not disobeyed, besides the Children of Israel, of beasts, animals, birds, insects, and trees, by withholding the rain from the Children of Israel." It is claimed—and Allah knows best—that Ilyas said: "My Lord, let me be the one who prays for them, and let me be the one who brings them relief from what they are in of the trial that has befallen them, perhaps they will return and desist from what they are upon of worshipping other than You." It was said to him: "Yes." So Ilyas came to the Children of Israel and said to them: "You have perished from hunger, and the beasts, animals, birds, insects, and trees have perished because of your sins, and you are upon falsehood and delusion," or as he said to them, "If you wish to know this, and to know that Allah is angry with you for what you are upon, and that what I call you to is the truth, then go out with these idols of yours that you worship and claim are better than what I call you to. If they respond to you, then it is as you say; but if they do not act, you will know that you are upon falsehood, and you will desist, and I will pray to Allah and He will relieve you of what you are in of trial." They said: "You have been fair." So they went out with their idols, and with what they drew near to Allah with of their innovations which He does not accept, and they called upon them, but they did not respond to them, nor did they relieve them of what they were in of trial, until they recognized the misguidance and falsehood they were in. Then they said to Ilyas: "O Ilyas, we have perished, so pray to Allah for us." Ilyas prayed for them for relief from what they were in, and that they be given rain. A cloud came out like a shield by Allah's permission over the sea while they watched, then the clouds gathered toward it, then it poured, and He sent the rain, and it relieved them, their lands became green, and relief came to them from what they had been in of the trial. Yet they did not desist and did not return, and they remained upon the most wicked of what they had been upon. When Ilyas saw their disbelief, he asked his Lord to take him to Himself and relieve him of them. It was said to him, as they claim: "Look on such-and-such a day; go out on it to such-and-such a land, and whatever comes to you, mount it and do not give it away." Ilyas went out, and al-Yasa' ibn Akhtub went out with him, until when he was in the town mentioned to him, at the place he had been commanded, there came to him a horse of fire until it stood before him, and he leapt upon it and departed with it. Al-Yasa' called to him: "O Ilyas, O Ilyas, what do you command me?" That was the last of their contact with him. Allah clothed him with feathers, dressed him in light, cut off from him the pleasure of food and drink, and he flew among the angels. He was a human, angelic, earthly, and heavenly being.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest ones﴾. The majority of the readers of Mecca, Medina, and Basra, and some of the readers of Kufa, recited it: ﴿Allah, your Lord (Rabbukum) and the Lord (Rabbu) of your forefathers, the earliest ones﴾, with the nominative, as a new sentence, and that the statement ends at His words ﴿the best of creators﴾. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it: ﴿Allah, your Lord (Rabbakum) and the Lord (Raba) of your forefathers, the earliest ones﴾, with the accusative, as a response to His words ﴿and forsake the best of creators﴾, on the basis that all of it is one speech.

The correct view, in our opinion, is that these are two recitations close in meaning, and since both recitations are widely transmitted among the readers, whichever one the reader recites is correct. The meaning of the speech is: That is your object of worship, O people, which deserves worship from you: your Lord who created you, and the Lord of your forefathers who came before you, not the idol that creates nothing and neither harms nor benefits.

* *

As for His words, ﴿But they denied him, so indeed they will be brought forth [to punishment]﴾:

He says: Ilyas's people denied him, so indeed they will be brought forth: that is, they will be brought forth to the punishment of Allah, to witness it.

As reported:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿so indeed they will be brought forth﴾ to the punishment of Allah. ﴿except the chosen servants of Allah﴾ means: they will be brought forth to the punishment of Allah, except the servants of Allah whom He chose and saved from the punishment. ﴿And We left for him among later generations﴾ means: We left for him a good remembrance among the later nations after him.

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He: ﴿Peace be upon the family of Yasin. Thus do We reward the good-doers. Indeed, he was among Our believing servants.﴾**

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: a safety granted by Allah to the family of Yasin.

The reciters (qurra', those who transmit the established readings of the Qur'an) differed over the recitation of His words ﴿Peace be upon the family of Yasin﴾. The majority of the reciters of Makkah, Basra and Kufa recited it as ﴿سَلامُ عَلى إلْياسِينَ﴾, with a kasra on the alif of Ilyasin. Some of them said: it is the name Ilyas, and he was called by two names: Ilyas and Ilyasin, like Ibrahim and Ibrahim (Abraham). They supported this by pointing out that everywhere in the surah where ﴿سَلامٌ﴾ occurs it is a peace upon the prophet mentioned, not upon his family, so Ilyasin is likewise a peace upon Ilyas alone, not upon his family.

Some of the people of Arabic grammar (ahl al-'arabiyyah, the grammarians) said: Ilyas is a name from the Hebrew names, like their saying Isma'il and Ishaq, and the alif and lam are part of it. He said: If you made it Arabic, from al-ils, making it an if'al form like al-ikhraj and al-idkhal, it would be declined (ajra). He said: Yet he said ﴿سلام على إلياسين﴾, making it with a nun. Arabs do this with foreign names: they say Mikal, Mika'il and Mika'in (with a nun). In the tribe of Bani Asad they say: "This is Isma'in has come," while the rest of the Arabs say it with a lam. He said: Some of Bani Numayr recited to me a verse about a lizard that someone had hunted:

"The lord of the market said when we came: 'This, by the Lord of the House, is Isra'ina.'"

This is the basis for the reading ﴿إلياسين﴾. Abu 'Ubaydah (the philologist, author of Majaz al-Qur'an) said: "Salam 'ala Ilyasin" means peace upon Ilyas and his household and upon all the people of his religion, without adding the ya' to the number. A poet said:

"Leave me to the victory of the two beloved ones, leave me."

So Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr made Abu Khubayb a diminutive, and whoever held his view counted them as a number and did not add the ya' to them, meaning he did not attribute them to him with the ya' of nisbah (relative adjective). So one says Khubayabiyyun. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: A caller called out on the day of al-Kilab, saying: "The Yazidun have perished," meaning Yazid ibn 'Abd al-Madan, Yazid ibn Hawbar and Yazid ibn Makhramah al-Harithiyyun. It is also said: "The Harithun and the Ash'arun have come to you."

He said: This is like His words, Ilyasin. He said: If you wish, you may take Ilyasin to be a plural, so that his companions enter into his name, as you say of a people whose leader is al-Muhallab: "The Muhallabah and the Muhallabun have come to you." This is like their saying al-Ash'arin and al-Sa'din, with the lightening, and the like. A poet said:

"I am the son of Sa'd, the lord of the Sa'dayn."

He (al-Farra') said, after his earlier statement that Ilyasin is a dialect form of Ilyas among Bani Asad: If you wish, you may take "Ilyasin" as a plural, making his companions enter into his name, as you say to a people whose leader is al-Muhallab: "The Muhallabah and the Muhallabun have come to you," so it is like His words: al-Ash'arin and al-Sa'din and the like.

He said: In the case of two, it is that one of them is joined to his companion when he is more famous by name, as a poet said:

"The two Zahdams repaid me with an evil recompense, though I was a man who is repaid with generosity."

The name of one of them is Zahdam. Another said:

"May Allah repay the two one-eyed men (al-A'war) with a cursed obligation, and Farwah, the ... of the bull's rump, the crooked-mouthed."

The name of one of them is A'war.

The majority of the reciters of Madinah recited it as ﴿سَلام عَلى آل يَاسِينَ﴾, with the separation of Al from Yasin, and some of them interpreted it to mean: peace upon the family of Muhammad (ﷺ).

It is related from some reciters that he recited ﴿وَإِنَّ إِلْيَاسَ﴾ without the hamza in Ilyas, making the alif and lam attached to "Yas" for definiteness, and he said: his name was originally "Yas", to which an alif and lam were added. Then he would recite accordingly: "Peace upon Ilyasin."

The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, is the recitation of the one who recited ﴿سَلامٌ عَلَى إِلْ يَاسِينَ﴾ with a kasra on its alif, on the pattern of Idrasin, because Allah, exalted is His remembrance, in every place in this surah where He mentions a prophet of His prophets, may Allah's blessings be upon them, reports that peace is upon him, not upon his family. So the peace in this place should likewise be upon Ilyas, as His peace upon others of His prophets, not upon his family, in the manner of what we have explained of that meaning.

If someone thinks that Ilyasin is other than Ilyas, then in what we have related of the arguments of those who argued that Ilyasin is Ilyas, there is sufficiency without adding to it.

Moreover, among what has come down:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Peace be upon the family of Yasin﴾: he said: Ilyas.

In the recitation of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, "Salam 'ala Idrasin," there is clear evidence of the error of the one who said that it means peace upon the family of Muhammad, and of the corruption of the recitation of the one who recited "wa-inna Ilyasa" by joining the nun of "inna" to "Ilyas," and directing the alif and lam to them as definite markers of the name "Yas." That is because Abdullah used to say that Ilyas is Idris, and he would recite "wa-inna Idrisa la-mina al-mursalin," and then recite accordingly "Salam 'ala Idrasin," just as the others recited ﴿سَلامٌ عَلَى إِلْ يَاسِينَ﴾ with the separation of "Al" from "Yasin." A parallel to naming Ilyas as "Il Yasin" is His words: ﴿and a tree that grows out of Mount Sinai﴾ [and He said in another place: ﴿and Mount Sinin﴾], and it is one place named thus.

* *

As for His words ﴿Thus do We reward the good-doers﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Thus do We reward the people of obedience to Us and those who do good in their deeds. As for His words ﴿Indeed, he was among Our believing servants﴾, He says: Indeed Ilyas was one of Our servants who believed, so they affirmed Our oneness, obeyed Us, and did not associate anything with Us.

The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, is the recitation of the one who recited ﴿سَلامٌ عَلَى إِلْ يَاسِينَ﴾ with a kasra on its alif, on the pattern of Idrasin, because Allah, exalted is His remembrance, in every place in this surah where He mentions a prophet of His prophets, may Allah's blessings be upon them, reports that peace is upon him, not upon his family. So the peace in this place should likewise be upon Ilyas, as His peace upon others of His prophets, not upon his family, in the manner of what we have explained of that meaning.

If someone thinks that Ilyasin is other than Ilyas, then in what we have related of the arguments of those who argued that Ilyasin is Ilyas, there is sufficiency without adding to it.

Moreover, among what has come down:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Peace be upon the family of Yasin﴾: he said: Ilyas.

In the recitation of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, "Salam 'ala Idrasin," there is clear evidence of the error of the one who said that it means peace upon the family of Muhammad, and of the corruption of the recitation of the one who recited "wa-inna Ilyasa" by joining the nun of "inna" to "Ilyas," and directing the alif and lam to them as definite markers of the name "Yas." That is because Abdullah used to say that Ilyas is Idris, and he would recite "wa-inna Idrisa la-mina al-mursalin," and then recite accordingly "Salam 'ala Idrasin," just as the others recited ﴿سَلامٌ عَلَى إِلْ يَاسِينَ﴾ with the separation of "Al" from "Yasin." A parallel to naming Ilyas as "Il Yasin" is His words: ﴿and a tree that grows out of Mount Sinai﴾ [and He said in another place: ﴿and Mount Sinin﴾], and it is one place named thus.

* *

As for His words ﴿Thus do We reward the good-doers﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Thus do We reward the people of obedience to Us and those who do good in their deeds. As for His words ﴿Indeed, he was among Our believing servants﴾, He says: Indeed Ilyas was one of Our servants who believed, so they affirmed Our oneness, obeyed Us, and did not associate anything with Us.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verses 133–136:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed Lot was among the messengers. (133) When We saved him and his family, all of them, (134) except an old woman among those who remained behind. (135) Then We destroyed the others.﴾ (136)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "And indeed Lot was among the messengers" means: Lot was a messenger from among the messengers.

﴿When We saved him and his family, all of them﴾ means: when We saved Lot and his family, all of them, from the punishment which We brought down upon his people, thereby destroying them. ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾ means: except an old woman among those who remained behind, and she was the wife of Lot. We have already mentioned her account earlier, and the differences of those who differ regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿among those who remained behind﴾, and the correct view on that according to us.

* It has been related to me from al-Musayyib ibn Sharik, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾, that he said: except his wife, who stayed behind and was turned into a stone, and she was called Hayshaf‑ [[In ʿAra'is al-Majalis of al-Tha'labi, Halabi edition, p. 106: "and she was called Halsaf".]]

* Muhammad related to us, he said: Ahmad related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾, he said: "the ones who were destroyed."

* * *

As for His saying ﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾:

It means: Then We rained down stones upon them from above, thereby destroying them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 137–139:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning﴾ [37:137] ﴿and at night. Will you not then use reason?﴾ [37:138]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the polytheists of Quraysh: "And indeed, you pass by the people of Lot, whom We destroyed, at your morning time by day and by night."

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning﴾: They said, "Yes, by Allah, in the morning and in the evening, you tread upon it with treading. Whoever takes the road from Medina to Syria takes the route past Sodom, the town of the people of Lot."

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿you pass by them in the morning﴾: He said, "In your journeys."

* * *

As for His saying ﴿Will you not then use reason?﴾

He says: "Do you not have minds with which you reflect and contemplate, so that you would know that whoever among the servants of Allah follows the path of those who disbelieve in Him and deny His messengers, like the path of these people described as the people of Lot, there descends upon them a punishment from Allah like what descended upon them for their disbelief in Allah and their denial of His Messenger? That would deter you from what you are upon of associating others with Allah and denying Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him."

As related:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Will you not then use reason?﴾: "Will you not reflect on what befell them for their disobedience to Allah, lest there befall you what befell them?" He said: "And that passing is that you pass by them."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 140–142:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers (139). When he fled to the laden ship (140). And he cast lots, and was among the losers (141). Then the whale swallowed him, while he was blameworthy (142).﴾

He, the Exalted, says: And indeed, Jonah was one of the messengers sent to his people. ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾ means: when he ran away to the ship, which is the al-fulk, and the mashhun is the one filled with cargo, loaded down.

As related:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿to the laden ship﴾: "We used to narrate that it means the ship loaded down."

* Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿the laden ship﴾: He said: "The loaded down."

* * *

As for His saying ﴿and he cast lots﴾

It means: he drew lots (fa-qarra'a).

The people of interpretation said what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to us, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and he cast lots﴾: he said, "He drew lots (aqra'a)."

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and he cast lots, and was among the losers﴾: He said: "The ship was held back, so the people knew that it was held back because of an offence they had committed. So they cast lots, and Jonah was chosen by lot, so he threw himself down, and the whale swallowed him."

* Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿and he cast lots﴾: He said: "He drew lots."

* * *

As for His saying ﴿and was among the losers﴾

It means: he was among those who were chosen by lot and defeated. From this one says: "Allah made the argument of so-and-so fail (adhda'a), so it failed (dahadat)," meaning He nullified it and it became void. Al-dahd originally means slipping in water and mud. It has been reported of them: "dahada Allah hujjatahu," but it is rare.

The people of interpretation said what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿among the losers﴾: He said: "among those who were drawn against (al-maqru'in)."

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿among the losers﴾: He said: "among those who were cast lots against."

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿and was among the losers﴾: He said: "among those drawn against."

* * *

As for His saying ﴿Then the whale swallowed him﴾

It means: the whale swallowed him; it is an iftial form from al-laqm (swallowing).

* * *

As for His saying ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾

It means: while he had earned blame. It is said: "qad alama al-rajul" when a man commits something for which he deserves blame, even if he is not blamed, just as it is said: "asbahtu muhmiqan, mu'tashan" meaning you have foolishness and thirst. From this is the saying of Labid:

"You reproached me foolishly, and you blamed me though I was not blameworthy... and before today, one who was not wise guided you."

[The verse is by Labid ibn Rabi'ah al-Amiri. Abu Ubaydah cited it in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 211) saying, regarding His saying "while he was blameworthy": the Arabs say "alama fulan fi amrihi," meaning he came to a matter for which he is blamed. And Labid said: "safaha..." the verse. He also cited it in Lisan al-Arab (root l-w-m) in the same way as Abu Ubaydah, and said: "lam fulan ghayr muleem."]

As for the blamed (al-malum), he is one who is blamed by the tongue and reproached by speech.

The people of interpretation said what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to me, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾: He said: "one who is at fault."

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾: He said: "that is, in his action."

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾: He said: "He was at fault." He said: "al-Mulim is the one at fault."

It has been reported of them: "dahada Allah hujjatahu," but it is rare.

The people of interpretation said what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿among the losers﴾: He said: "among those who were drawn against (al-maqru'in)."

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿among the losers﴾: He said: "among those who were cast lots against."

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿and was among the losers﴾: He said: "among those drawn against."

* * *

As for His saying ﴿Then the whale swallowed him﴾

It means: the whale swallowed him; it is an iftial form from al-laqm (swallowing).

* * *

As for His saying ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾

It means: while he had earned blame. It is said: "qad alama al-rajul" when a man commits something for which he deserves blame, even if he is not blamed, just as it is said: "asbahtu muhmiqan, mu'tashan" meaning you have foolishness and thirst. From this is the saying of Labid:

"You reproached me foolishly, and you blamed me though I was not blameworthy... and before today, one who was not wise guided you."

[The verse is by Labid ibn Rabi'ah al-Amiri. Abu Ubaydah cited it in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 211) saying, regarding His saying "while he was blameworthy": the Arabs say "alama fulan fi amrihi," meaning he came to a matter for which he is blamed. And Labid said: "safaha..." the verse. He also cited it in Lisan al-Arab (root l-w-m) in the same way as Abu Ubaydah, and said: "lam fulan ghayr muleem."]

As for the blamed (al-malum), he is one who is blamed by the tongue and reproached by speech.

The people of interpretation said what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to me, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾: He said: "one who is at fault."

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾: He said: "that is, in his action."

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾: He said: "He was at fault." He said: "al-Mulim is the one at fault."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 37, verses 143–146:

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God) [al-musabbihin]﴾, meaning Yunus (Jonah), ﴿he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are raised﴾. He says: he would have remained in the belly of the fish, imprisoned, until the Day of Resurrection, the Day on which God raises His creation. But he had been one of those who remember God before the trial, so God remembered him during the trial, rescued him and delivered him.

The people of interpretation differ concerning the time of Yunus's glorifying of God, by which God mentioned him, when He said ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾. Some of them said something similar to what we have said about it, and they said the same as our view regarding the meaning of His words ﴿of those who glorify﴾.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾: he used to pray much in ease, so God rescued him by that. He said: It was said in wisdom (literature): good deeds lift up their doer when he stumbles, and when he is thrown down he finds something to lean on.

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from one of his companions, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾: he said: he prayed at length in ease. He said: Indeed good deeds lift up their doer when he stumbles; when he is thrown down, he finds something to lean on.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Dahr narrated to us, that Yazid al-Raqqashi related to him, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say, and I do not know except that Anas was raising it to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Yunus the Prophet, when it occurred to him to call upon God with the words when He called to him while he was in the belly of the fish, said: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers.' So the supplication ascended beneath the Throne. The angels said: 'O Lord, this is a weak voice, known in a distant land.' He said: 'Do you not know it?' They said: 'O Lord, who is it?' He said: 'That is My servant Yunus.' They said: 'Your servant Yunus, for whom a righteous deed has never ceased to be raised and whose supplication is answered?' They said: 'O Lord, will he not be shown mercy for what he used to do in ease, so that You deliver him from the trial?' He said: 'Yes.' So He commanded the fish, and it cast him onto the open land."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾: he said: "of those who pray."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾: he said: "of those who pray."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾: he said: he had a righteous deed in the past.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿of those who glorify﴾: he said: "those who pray."

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Kathir ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Maymun ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Qays say from his pulpit: "Remember God in ease and He will remember you in hardship. Indeed Yunus was a servant of God who remembered Him. When hardship befell him, he called upon God, and God said: ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God), he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are raised﴾. So He reminded him of what he had done. And Pharaoh was arrogant and oppressive, until ﴿drowning overtook him, he said: 'I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the submitters.' 'Now? And you had disobeyed before and been of the corrupters?'﴾" Al-Dahhak said: So remember God in ease and He will remember you in hardship.

Abu Ja'far said: It was said that what God mentioned of him, ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾, was the prayer he performed inside the belly of the fish.

Others said: That was glorification (tasbih), not prayer.

Those who said this:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: 'Imran al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say regarding His words ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾: "By God, it was only a prayer he initiated in the belly of the fish." 'Imran said: I mentioned that to Qatadah, and he denied it and said: "By God, he used to pray much in ease."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from al-Mughirah ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy﴾. He said: he said ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers﴾. When he said it, the fish cast him out, and he was sick.

The people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are raised﴾: the belly of the fish would have become a grave for him until the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, who said: Yunus remained in the belly of the fish for forty days.

* *

As for His words ﴿So We cast him onto the open land﴾:

He says: We threw him out onto the open expanse of the earth, where nothing, neither tree nor anything else, screened him. From this is the saying of the poet:

"And I raised a leg whose stumbling I do not fear, and cast my garments in the open land."

[The verse is among the witnesses of Abu 'Ubaydah in "Majaz al-Qur'an," p. 211b. He said regarding God's words "then We cast him onto the open land": the Arabs say "I cast him onto the open land," meaning the empty ground. Al-Khuza'i said: "And I raised a leg..." The line. The open land: nothing screens it of tree or anything else. The author of (al-Lisan: 'ara) cited it without attributing it. He said: Abu 'Ubaydah said it is called 'ara' only because there is no tree in it and nothing covers it. It was also said: the open land is the bare surface of the earth. And he cited: "And raised him, a leg..." The line. After that he transmitted the words of al-Zajjaj on the meaning of "ara'," so refer to them there.]

He means by "the land" (al-balad): the open expanse.

The people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to me, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿So We cast him onto the open land﴾: he said: "We threw him onto the shore."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿So We cast him onto the open land﴾: "in a land where there was nothing and no vegetation."

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿onto the open land﴾: he said: "onto the earth."

* *

As for His words ﴿while he was ailing﴾:

He says: while he was like a newborn child, raw flesh.

As:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿while he was ailing﴾: "in the likeness of a child."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Salamah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The fish carried him out until it expelled him on the shore of the sea, and it cast him out like a newborn child, with nothing lacking from his creation.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: The fish did not expel him until he became like a newborn child, the flesh and bone having been torn, so he became like a newborn child; and it cast him in a place, and God caused a gourd plant to grow over him.

* *

As for His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We caused to grow over Yunus a tree of those trees that do not stand on a stalk. Every tree that does not stand on a stalk, like the gourd, the watermelon, the colocynth and the like, is among the Arabs called yaqtin.

The people of interpretation differed about this. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: it is everything that grows on the surface of the earth without a stalk.

Mutar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: al-Asbagh ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: everything that grows and then dies within its year.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "a plant of gourd": they said in his presence: the pumpkin. He said: And what makes it more deserving than the watermelon?

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿a plant of gourd﴾: he said: "one without a root, of the pumpkin or something similar."

Others said: it is the pumpkin (qar').

Those who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: "the pumpkin."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abd Allah, that he said regarding this verse ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: "the pumpkin."

Mutar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: "the pumpkin."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: "We used to narrate that it is the gourd (dubba'), this pumpkin that you have seen, which God caused to grow over him, and he would eat from it."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr narrated to me, saying: Ibn Qusayt narrated to me, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: He was cast onto the open land, and God caused a gourd vine to grow over him. We said: "O Abu Hurayrah, what is the yaqtinah?" He said: "The tree, the gourd (dubba'). God made ready for him a wild doe that grazed on the low plants of the earth, so it would spread itself over him and give him its milk to drink every evening and morning, until he grew strong." And Ibn Abi al-Salt said before Islam, in this regard, a verse of poetry:

"So He caused a gourd to grow over him, by mercy from God; had it not been for God, he would have been found exposed to the sun."

[The verse is by Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt, as the author said, but I did not find it among the Christian poets nor in his biography in al-Aghani. Abu 'Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an (p. 211b), regarding "a tree of yaqtin": every tree that does not stand on a stalk is yaqtin, like the gourd, the colocynth and the watermelon. End. In (al-Lisan: qatan): al-Farra' said: it was said in the presence of Ibn 'Abbas that it is the leaf of the pumpkin; and the pumpkin was not singled out from among trees as yaqtin; every leaf that spreads out and expands is yaqtin. Al-Farra' said: Mujahid said: everything that spreads flat on the ground is yaqtin. Al-Kalbi said something similar. He said: among them is the pumpkin, the watermelon, the cucumber and the shiryan. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: everything that grows and then dies within its year is yaqtin. End.]

Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, saying: Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Mughirah, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: the pumpkin.

It was reported from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿a plant of gourd﴾: the pumpkin.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: God caused a plant of gourd to grow over him. He said: He would not take a leaf from it that he picked, except that it gave him milk to drink, or he said: he drank from it whatever he wished until he grew strong.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿a plant of gourd﴾: he said: it is the pumpkin, and the Arabs call it al-dubba'.

'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding God's words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: it is the pumpkin.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: the pumpkin.

Others said: the yaqtin was a tree that shaded Yunus.

Those who said this:

al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Thabit ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The yaqtin is a tree that God named yaqtin, which shaded him, and it is not the pumpkin. He said: It is related that God sent upon him the beast of the earth, which began to gnaw at its roots, and its leaves began to fall, until the sun reached him, and he complained of it. (God) said: "O Yunus, you grew distressed by the heat of the sun, yet you did not grieve for a hundred thousand or more who repented to Me, so I accepted their repentance?"
