Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Salamah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The fish carried him out until it expelled him on the shore of the sea, and it cast him out like a newborn child, with nothing lacking from his creation.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: The fish did not expel him until he became like a newborn child, the flesh and bone having been torn, so he became like a newborn child; and it cast him in a place, and God caused a gourd plant to grow over him.

* *

As for His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We caused to grow over Yunus a tree of those trees that do not stand on a stalk. Every tree that does not stand on a stalk, like the gourd, the watermelon, the colocynth and the like, is among the Arabs called yaqtin.

The people of interpretation differed about this. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: it is everything that grows on the surface of the earth without a stalk.

Mutar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: al-Asbagh ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: everything that grows and then dies within its year.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "a plant of gourd": they said in his presence: the pumpkin. He said: And what makes it more deserving than the watermelon?

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿a plant of gourd﴾: he said: "one without a root, of the pumpkin or something similar."

Others said: it is the pumpkin (qar').

Those who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: "the pumpkin."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abd Allah, that he said regarding this verse ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: "the pumpkin."

Mutar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: "the pumpkin."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: "We used to narrate that it is the gourd (dubba'), this pumpkin that you have seen, which God caused to grow over him, and he would eat from it."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr narrated to me, saying: Ibn Qusayt narrated to me, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: He was cast onto the open land, and God caused a gourd vine to grow over him. We said: "O Abu Hurayrah, what is the yaqtinah?" He said: "The tree, the gourd (dubba'). God made ready for him a wild doe that grazed on the low plants of the earth, so it would spread itself over him and give him its milk to drink every evening and morning, until he grew strong." And Ibn Abi al-Salt said before Islam, in this regard, a verse of poetry:

"So He caused a gourd to grow over him, by mercy from God; had it not been for God, he would have been found exposed to the sun."

[The verse is by Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt, as the author said, but I did not find it among the Christian poets nor in his biography in al-Aghani. Abu 'Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an (p. 211b), regarding "a tree of yaqtin": every tree that does not stand on a stalk is yaqtin, like the gourd, the colocynth and the watermelon. End. In (al-Lisan: qatan): al-Farra' said: it was said in the presence of Ibn 'Abbas that it is the leaf of the pumpkin; and the pumpkin was not singled out from among trees as yaqtin; every leaf that spreads out and expands is yaqtin. Al-Farra' said: Mujahid said: everything that spreads flat on the ground is yaqtin. Al-Kalbi said something similar. He said: among them is the pumpkin, the watermelon, the cucumber and the shiryan. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: everything that grows and then dies within its year is yaqtin. End.]

Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, saying: Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Mughirah, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: the pumpkin.

It was reported from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿a plant of gourd﴾: the pumpkin.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: God caused a plant of gourd to grow over him. He said: He would not take a leaf from it that he picked, except that it gave him milk to drink, or he said: he drank from it whatever he wished until he grew strong.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿a plant of gourd﴾: he said: it is the pumpkin, and the Arabs call it al-dubba'.

'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding God's words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: it is the pumpkin.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: the pumpkin.

Others said: the yaqtin was a tree that shaded Yunus.

Those who said this:

al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Thabit ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The yaqtin is a tree that God named yaqtin, which shaded him, and it is not the pumpkin. He said: It is related that God sent upon him the beast of the earth, which began to gnaw at its roots, and its leaves began to fall, until the sun reached him, and he complained of it. (God) said: "O Yunus, you grew distressed by the heat of the sun, yet you did not grieve for a hundred thousand or more who repented to Me, so I accepted their repentance?"

He says: he would have remained in the belly of the fish, imprisoned, until the Day of Resurrection, the Day on which God raises His creation. But he had been one of those who remember God before the trial, so God remembered him during the trial, rescued him and delivered him.

The people of interpretation differ concerning the time of Yunus's glorifying of God, by which God mentioned him, when He said ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾. Some of them said something similar to what we have said about it, and they said the same as our view regarding the meaning of His words ﴿of those who glorify﴾.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾: he used to pray much in ease, so God rescued him by that. He said: It was said in wisdom (literature): good deeds lift up their doer when he stumbles, and when he is thrown down he finds something to lean on.

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from one of his companions, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾: he said: he prayed at length in ease. He said: Indeed good deeds lift up their doer when he stumbles; when he is thrown down, he finds something to lean on.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Dahr narrated to us, that Yazid al-Raqqashi related to him, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say, and I do not know except that Anas was raising it to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Yunus the Prophet, when it occurred to him to call upon God with the words when He called to him while he was in the belly of the fish, said: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers.' So the supplication ascended beneath the Throne. The angels said: 'O Lord, this is a weak voice, known in a distant land.' He said: 'Do you not know it?' They said: 'O Lord, who is it?' He said: 'That is My servant Yunus.' They said: 'Your servant Yunus, for whom a righteous deed has never ceased to be raised and whose supplication is answered?' They said: 'O Lord, will he not be shown mercy for what he used to do in ease, so that You deliver him from the trial?' He said: 'Yes.' So He commanded the fish, and it cast him onto the open land."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾: he said: "of those who pray."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾: he said: "of those who pray."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾: he said: he had a righteous deed in the past.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿of those who glorify﴾: he said: "those who pray."

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Kathir ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Maymun ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Qays say from his pulpit: "Remember God in ease and He will remember you in hardship. Indeed Yunus was a servant of God who remembered Him. When hardship befell him, he called upon God, and God said: ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God), he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are raised﴾. So He reminded him of what he had done. And Pharaoh was arrogant and oppressive, until ﴿drowning overtook him, he said: 'I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the submitters.' 'Now? And you had disobeyed before and been of the corrupters?'﴾" Al-Dahhak said: So remember God in ease and He will remember you in hardship.

Abu Ja'far said: It was said that what God mentioned of him, ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾, was the prayer he performed inside the belly of the fish.

Others said: That was glorification (tasbih), not prayer.

Those who said this:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: 'Imran al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say regarding His words ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾: "By God, it was only a prayer he initiated in the belly of the fish." 'Imran said: I mentioned that to Qatadah, and he denied it and said: "By God, he used to pray much in ease."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from al-Mughirah ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy﴾. He said: he said ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers﴾. When he said it, the fish cast him out, and he was sick.

The people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are raised﴾: the belly of the fish would have become a grave for him until the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, who said: Yunus remained in the belly of the fish for forty days.

* *

As for His words ﴿So We cast him onto the open land﴾:

He says: We threw him out onto the open expanse of the earth, where nothing, neither tree nor anything else, screened him. From this is the saying of the poet:

"And I raised a leg whose stumbling I do not fear, and cast my garments in the open land."

[The verse is among the witnesses of Abu 'Ubaydah in "Majaz al-Qur'an," p. 211b. He said regarding God's words "then We cast him onto the open land": the Arabs say "I cast him onto the open land," meaning the empty ground. Al-Khuza'i said: "And I raised a leg..." The line. The open land: nothing screens it of tree or anything else. The author of (al-Lisan: 'ara) cited it without attributing it. He said: Abu 'Ubaydah said it is called 'ara' only because there is no tree in it and nothing covers it. It was also said: the open land is the bare surface of the earth. And he cited: "And raised him, a leg..." The line. After that he transmitted the words of al-Zajjaj on the meaning of "ara'," so refer to them there.]

He means by "the land" (al-balad): the open expanse.

The people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to me, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿So We cast him onto the open land﴾: he said: "We threw him onto the shore."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿So We cast him onto the open land﴾: "in a land where there was nothing and no vegetation."

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿onto the open land﴾: he said: "onto the earth."

* *

As for His words ﴿while he was ailing﴾:

He says: while he was like a newborn child, raw flesh.

So He reminded him of what he had done. And Pharaoh was arrogant and oppressive, until ﴿drowning overtook him, he said: 'I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the submitters.' 'Now? And you had disobeyed before and been of the corrupters?'﴾" Al-Dahhak said: So remember God in ease and He will remember you in hardship.

Abu Ja'far said: It was said that what God mentioned of him, ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾, was the prayer he performed inside the belly of the fish.

Others said: That was glorification (tasbih), not prayer.

Those who said this:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: 'Imran al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say regarding His words ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (God)﴾: "By God, it was only a prayer he initiated in the belly of the fish." 'Imran said: I mentioned that to Qatadah, and he denied it and said: "By God, he used to pray much in ease."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from al-Mughirah ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy﴾. He said: he said ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers﴾. When he said it, the fish cast him out, and he was sick.

The people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are raised﴾: the belly of the fish would have become a grave for him until the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, who said: Yunus remained in the belly of the fish for forty days.

* *

As for His words ﴿So We cast him onto the open land﴾:

He says: We threw him out onto the open expanse of the earth, where nothing, neither tree nor anything else, screened him. From this is the saying of the poet:

"And I raised a leg whose stumbling I do not fear, and cast my garments in the open land."

[The verse is among the witnesses of Abu 'Ubaydah in "Majaz al-Qur'an," p. 211b. He said regarding God's words "then We cast him onto the open land": the Arabs say "I cast him onto the open land," meaning the empty ground. Al-Khuza'i said: "And I raised a leg..." The line. The open land: nothing screens it of tree or anything else. The author of (al-Lisan: 'ara) cited it without attributing it. He said: Abu 'Ubaydah said it is called 'ara' only because there is no tree in it and nothing covers it. It was also said: the open land is the bare surface of the earth. And he cited: "And raised him, a leg..." The line. After that he transmitted the words of al-Zajjaj on the meaning of "ara'," so refer to them there.]

He means by "the land" (al-balad): the open expanse.

The people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to me, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿So We cast him onto the open land﴾: he said: "We threw him onto the shore."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿So We cast him onto the open land﴾: "in a land where there was nothing and no vegetation."

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿onto the open land﴾: he said: "onto the earth."

* *

As for His words ﴿while he was ailing﴾:

He says: while he was like a newborn child, raw flesh.

As:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿while he was ailing﴾: "in the likeness of a child."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Salamah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The fish carried him out until it expelled him on the shore of the sea, and it cast him out like a newborn child, with nothing lacking from his creation.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: The fish did not expel him until he became like a newborn child, the flesh and bone having been torn, so he became like a newborn child; and it cast him in a place, and God caused a gourd plant to grow over him.

* *

As for His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We caused to grow over Yunus a tree of those trees that do not stand on a stalk. Every tree that does not stand on a stalk, like the gourd, the watermelon, the colocynth and the like, is among the Arabs called yaqtin.

The people of interpretation differed about this. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: it is everything that grows on the surface of the earth without a stalk.

Mutar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: al-Asbagh ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: everything that grows and then dies within its year.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "a plant of gourd": they said in his presence: the pumpkin. He said: And what makes it more deserving than the watermelon?

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿a plant of gourd﴾: he said: "one without a root, of the pumpkin or something similar."

Others said: it is the pumpkin (qar').

Those who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: "the pumpkin."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abd Allah, that he said regarding this verse ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: "the pumpkin."

Mutar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: "the pumpkin."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: "We used to narrate that it is the gourd (dubba'), this pumpkin that you have seen, which God caused to grow over him, and he would eat from it."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr narrated to me, saying: Ibn Qusayt narrated to me, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: He was cast onto the open land, and God caused a gourd vine to grow over him. We said: "O Abu Hurayrah, what is the yaqtinah?" He said: "The tree, the gourd (dubba'). God made ready for him a wild doe that grazed on the low plants of the earth, so it would spread itself over him and give him its milk to drink every evening and morning, until he grew strong." And Ibn Abi al-Salt said before Islam, in this regard, a verse of poetry:

"So He caused a gourd to grow over him, by mercy from God; had it not been for God, he would have been found exposed to the sun."

[The verse is by Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt, as the author said, but I did not find it among the Christian poets nor in his biography in al-Aghani. Abu 'Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an (p. 211b), regarding "a tree of yaqtin": every tree that does not stand on a stalk is yaqtin, like the gourd, the colocynth and the watermelon. End. In (al-Lisan: qatan): al-Farra' said: it was said in the presence of Ibn 'Abbas that it is the leaf of the pumpkin; and the pumpkin was not singled out from among trees as yaqtin; every leaf that spreads out and expands is yaqtin. Al-Farra' said: Mujahid said: everything that spreads flat on the ground is yaqtin. Al-Kalbi said something similar. He said: among them is the pumpkin, the watermelon, the cucumber and the shiryan. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: everything that grows and then dies within its year is yaqtin. End.]

Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, saying: Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Mughirah, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: the pumpkin.

It was reported from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿a plant of gourd﴾: the pumpkin.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: God caused a plant of gourd to grow over him. He said: He would not take a leaf from it that he picked, except that it gave him milk to drink, or he said: he drank from it whatever he wished until he grew strong.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿a plant of gourd﴾: he said: it is the pumpkin, and the Arabs call it al-dubba'.

'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding God's words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: it is the pumpkin.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him﴾: he said: the pumpkin.

Others said: the yaqtin was a tree that shaded Yunus.

Those who said this:

al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Thabit ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The yaqtin is a tree that God named yaqtin, which shaded him, and it is not the pumpkin. He said: It is related that God sent upon him the beast of the earth, which began to gnaw at its roots, and its leaves began to fall, until the sun reached him, and he complained of it. (God) said: "O Yunus, you grew distressed by the heat of the sun, yet you did not grieve for a hundred thousand or more who repented to Me, so I accepted their repentance?"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verses 147–149:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more (147). So they believed, and We granted them enjoyment for a time (148). Then ask them: Has your Lord daughters while they have sons? (149)﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "We sent Yunus to a hundred thousand people, or more than a hundred thousand." It has been related from Ibn Abbas that he would say: the meaning of His saying ﴿or﴾ is "rather, they were more."

Mention of the narration to this effect:

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from al-Hakam ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Azwar, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾, he said: "Rather, they were more; they were a hundred thousand and thirty thousand."

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿a hundred thousand or more﴾, he said: "They were more by seventy thousand, and the punishment had been sent down upon them. When they separated the women from their children, and the beasts from their young, and they cried out to Allah, the punishment was lifted from them, and the sky rained blood."

* Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi related to me, saying: Amr ibn Abi Salamah related to us, saying: I heard Zuhayr, from one who heard Abu al-Aliyah, saying: Ubayy ibn Ka'b related to me, that he asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about His saying ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾, and he said: "They were more by twenty thousand."

Some of the Arabic grammarians of Basra used to say about this: its meaning is "to a hundred thousand, or they were more in your estimation," i.e., "thus they were in your estimation."

What is meant by His saying ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ is that He sent him to his people whom He had threatened with punishment; when it overshadowed them, they repented, and Allah lifted it from them. It was also said: they were the people of Nineveh.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾: He was sent to the people of Nineveh in the land of Mosul. He said: Al-Hasan said: Allah sent him before what befell him occurred. ﴿So they believed, and We granted them enjoyment for a time﴾.

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿to a hundred thousand or more﴾: They were the people of Yunus to whom he was sent before the fish swallowed him.

It was also said: Yunus was sent to the people of Nineveh after the fish had cast him out onto the bare ground.

Mention of those who said this:

* al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: I heard Abu Hilal Muhammad ibn Sulayman say: Shahr ibn Hawshab related to us, saying: (Jibril came to him, meaning Yunus, and said: "Go to the people of Nineveh and warn them that the punishment has come upon them." He said: "Let me seek a mount." He said: "The matter is more urgent than that." He said: "Let me seek a sandal." He said: "The matter is more urgent than that." So he became angry and went to the ship and boarded it. When he boarded, the ship was held back, neither advancing nor retreating. He said: "So they cast lots," and the lot fell upon him. Then the fish came, wagging its tail, and it was called out to the fish: "O fish, We did not make Yunus a provision for you; We only made you a shelter and a place of worship for him." So the fish swallowed him, and carried him from that place until it passed by al-Aylah, then carried him until it passed by the Tigris, then carried him until it cast him at Nineveh.)

* al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abu Hilal related to us, saying: Shahr ibn Hawshab related to us, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Yunus's mission was only after the fish had cast him out.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿So they believed﴾:

It means: they affirmed Allah, the One who sent Yunus to them, and they accepted the truth of what Yunus brought them from Allah.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿and We granted them enjoyment for a time﴾:

It means: We delayed the punishment from them, and We granted them enjoyment for a time, by their living until the reaching of their appointed terms of death.

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and We granted them enjoyment for a time﴾: death.

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿and We granted them enjoyment for a time﴾: death.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿Then ask them﴾:

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ask them, O Muhammad, the polytheists of your people from Quraysh.

As related:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Then ask them: Has your Lord daughters while they have sons?﴾: meaning the polytheists of Quraysh.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿Then ask them: Has your Lord daughters while they have sons?﴾: "Ask them." And he recited: ﴿And they ask you for a ruling﴾, meaning: they ask you.

* Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Then ask them﴾: he says: O Muhammad, ask them.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿Has your Lord daughters while they have sons?﴾:

It is mentioned that the polytheists of Quraysh used to say: the angels are daughters of Allah, and they used to worship them. So Allah said to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Ask them, and say to them: "Has your Lord daughters while you have sons?"

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Has your Lord daughters while they have sons?﴾: because they said, meaning the polytheists of Quraysh: for Allah are the daughters, and for themselves the sons.

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿So ask them: Has your Lord daughters while they have sons?﴾: he said: they used to worship the angels.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾: He was sent to the people of Nineveh in the land of Mosul. He said: Al-Hasan said: Allah sent him before what befell him occurred. ﴿So they believed, and We granted them enjoyment for a time﴾.

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿to a hundred thousand or more﴾: They were the people of Yunus to whom he was sent before the fish swallowed him.

It was also said: Yunus was sent to the people of Nineveh after the fish had cast him out onto the bare ground.

Mention of those who said this:

* al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: I heard Abu Hilal Muhammad ibn Sulayman say: Shahr ibn Hawshab related to us, saying: (Jibril came to him, meaning Yunus, and said: "Go to the people of Nineveh and warn them that the punishment has come upon them." He said: "Let me seek a mount." He said: "The matter is more urgent than that." He said: "Let me seek a sandal." He said: "The matter is more urgent than that." So he became angry and went to the ship and boarded it. When he boarded, the ship was held back, neither advancing nor retreating. He said: "So they cast lots," and the lot fell upon him. Then the fish came, wagging its tail, and it was called out to the fish: "O fish, We did not make Yunus a provision for you; We only made you a shelter and a place of worship for him." So the fish swallowed him, and carried him from that place until it passed by al-Aylah, then carried him until it passed by the Tigris, then carried him until it cast him at Nineveh.)

* al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abu Hilal related to us, saying: Shahr ibn Hawshab related to us, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Yunus's mission was only after the fish had cast him out.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿So they believed﴾:

* * *

As for His saying ﴿and We granted them enjoyment for a time﴾:

It means: We delayed the punishment from them, and We granted them enjoyment for a time, by their living until the reaching of their appointed terms of death.

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and We granted them enjoyment for a time﴾: death.

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿and We granted them enjoyment for a time﴾: death.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿Then ask them﴾:

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ask them, O Muhammad, the polytheists of your people from Quraysh.

As related:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Then ask them: Has your Lord daughters while they have sons?﴾: meaning the polytheists of Quraysh.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿Then ask them: Has your Lord daughters while they have sons?﴾: "Ask them." And he recited: ﴿And they ask you for a ruling﴾, meaning: they ask you.

* Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Then ask them﴾: he says: O Muhammad, ask them.

* * *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 37, verses 153–157:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons?﴾

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons? What is the matter with you? How do you judge? Will you not then take heed? Or do you have a clear authority? So bring your Book, if you are truthful.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, rebuking those Meccan polytheists who claimed that God has daughters: ﴿Has He chosen﴾ God, O people, ﴿daughters over sons﴾? The Arabs, when they direct the interrogative toward rebuke, sometimes retain the interrogative alif and sometimes drop it, as it has been said: ﴿Have you used up your good things in your worldly life?﴾ [46:20], read with the alif of interrogation and without it, and the meaning is one in both cases. When the interrogative is not used in His saying ﴿Has He chosen daughters﴾, the alif of (ightaṭā, "has chosen") is dropped in connected speech, and one begins with it with a kasra; when the interrogative is used, it is pronounced with a fatha and is cut off (pronounced as a hamzat al-qat').

It has been reported from some people of Medina that they recited this without the interrogative and without connection. As for the readers of Kufa and Basra, they follow the reading with the interrogative, with the alif pronounced with a fatha in all circumstances, and this is the reading we choose, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾

He says: What an evil judgment you pass, O people, that God should have daughters and you should have sons, while you yourselves do not approve of daughters for yourselves, so do you assign to Him what you do not approve for yourselves?

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾: He says: How can He assign to you sons and take daughters for Himself? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾

He says: Will you not reflect on what you say, so that you would recognize its error and desist from saying it?

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Or do you have a clear authority?﴾

He says: Do you have a proof whose soundness is clear to whoever hears it, establishing the truth of what you say?

As it was said:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Or do you have a clear authority?﴾: i.e., a clear excuse.

Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿clear authority﴾: he said, a proof.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿So bring your Book﴾

He says: Bring your proof from a Book that has come to you from God, showing that what you say, that He has daughters and you have sons, is as you claim.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So bring your Book﴾: i.e., bring your excuse. ﴿If you are truthful﴾.

Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So bring your Book﴾ that this is so, that He has daughters and you have sons.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿if you are truthful﴾

He says: if you are truthful that you have a proof for this.

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship﴾

He, exalted is He, says: And these polytheists made between Allah and the jinn a kinship.

* Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding **﴿So indeed you and what you worship﴾** up to **﴿destined to burn in Hellfire﴾**, who said: "You cannot lead astray any of My servants by this falsehood of yours, except one who has taken you as allies through works of the Fire."

It has been said: **﴿bi-fatinin﴾** (tempters/misleaders) comes from *fatantu uftin*, and this is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. As for the people of Najd, they say *aftantuhu fa-ana aftanuhu*. It is reported from al-Hasan that he recited: "**illa man huwa salu al-jahim**" with a *damma* on the *lam* of **ṣāl**, and if he meant by this the plural, as the poet said:

*When Hatim was found to be my cousin,*
*he is our glory, of whom whoever speaks, all of them.*

[The verse is among the examples cited by al-Farra' in *Ma'ani al-Qur'an* (folio 275), without attributing it to anyone. He said: "It may be that you make *ṣalu* a plural, as you say: 'Among the men is he who is your brothers.' You take *huwa* to refer to the indefinite noun and make its verb plural, as the poet said: 'When Hatim...' and he did not say 'they spoke'. The best of this in Arabic, when you bring out the pronoun, is to make it agree with the meaning and the number, because you intend to specify the noun." End quote. And in Fath al-Qadir by al-Shawkani (4:403), in the commentary on His words **"illa man huwa salu al-jahim"**: The majority read **ṣāl** with a *kasra* on the *lam*, because it is a defective noun in construction; the *ya'* was dropped because of the meeting of two unvocalized letters, and it was taken to agree with the wording of *man*, and was made singular, as **huwa** is singular. Al-Hasan and Ibn Abi 'Abla read it with a *damma* on the *lam*, with a *waw* after it; and it is related from them that they read it with a *damma* on the *lam* without a *waw*. As for with the *waw*, it is the sound plural with *waw*, taking the meaning of *man*, and the plural *nun* was dropped because of the annexation. As for without the *waw*, it may be a plural, and the *waw* was dropped in writing as it was dropped in pronunciation; and it may be singular, in which case by right it should have a *kasra* on the *lam*. Al-Nahhas said: The body of exegetes say it is a solecism (*lahn*), because it is not permissible to say *hadha qadi al-Madina* ("this is the judge of Medina" in the wrong form). The meaning is that the unbelievers and what they worship cannot lead astray any of God's servants, except one who is among the people of the Fire, that is, who will enter it. End quote.]

He said: "**ajma'ina**" (all of them), and did not say "they spoke." It is said of men, "**man huwa ikhwatuka**" (among men is he who is your brothers), taking *huwa* to the unspecified noun and making its verb plural. This is one way, although other usage is more eloquent than it. But if he meant by it a single person, then according to the grammarians it is a solecism, because they consider it a solecism to say *hadha ram* or *hadha qadi*, unless he heard in that a reversed dialect from the Arabs, like their saying *shaku al-silah* and *shaki al-silah* (bearing arms), and *'atha* and *'athwa*, *'aqa* and *'aqwa*, so that it would be a dialect. But I have not heard anyone mention hearing that from the Arabs.

God Most High says: These polytheists of Quraysh used to say before Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent to them as a prophet: ﴿If only we had with us a reminder from the former peoples﴾, meaning a book sent down from heaven like the Torah and the Gospel, or a prophet who came to us like those who came to the Jews and Christians, ﴿we would surely have been servants of Allah﴾, those whom He has purified for His worship and chosen for His Paradise.

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said.

Those who said this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And indeed they used to say, "If only we had with us a reminder from the former peoples, we would surely have been sincere servants of Allah"﴾, he said: This community already said that before Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent: "If only we had a reminder from the former peoples, we would be sincere servants of Allah." But when Muhammad (ﷺ) came to them, they disbelieved in him. So they will come to know.

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿a reminder from the former peoples﴾, he said: These were people among the polytheist Arabs who said: "If only we had a book from the books of the former peoples, or knowledge of the former peoples came to us." He said: Muhammad has indeed come to you with that.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: The discourse returns to the former peoples, the people of polytheism: ﴿And indeed they used to say, "If only we had with us a reminder from the former peoples"﴾.

* It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿If only we had with us a reminder from the former peoples, we would surely have been sincere servants of Allah﴾: This is the saying of the polytheists of Makkah. So when the reminder of the former peoples and the knowledge of the latter ones came to them, they disbelieved in it. So they will come to know.

Commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks (165), and indeed We are those who glorify [Him] (166), and indeed they used to say (167), "If only we had with us a reminder from the former peoples (168), we would surely have been sincere servants of Allah" (169).﴾

God Most High says, reporting the words of His angels: ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks﴾ for Allah, in worship of Him, ﴿and indeed We are those who glorify [Him]﴾, meaning those who pray to Him.

The report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) agrees with what we have said, and the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) held the same view.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq al-Marwazi narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid related to us, saying: Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say regarding His words ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks, and indeed We are those who glorify [Him]﴾: Masruq ibn al-Ajda' narrated from A'isha that she said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no place of a foot in the lowest heaven except that an angel is upon it, either prostrating or standing." That is the saying of Allah: ﴿And there is none of us but has a known station. And indeed We are those who stand in ranks, and indeed We are those who glorify [Him]﴾.

* Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya related to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, who said: Abdullah said: Indeed, among the heavens there is a heaven in which there is no place the size of a span except that upon it is the forehead of an angel or his foot standing; he said: Then he recited: ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks, and indeed We are those who glorify [Him]﴾.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abdullah, who said: Indeed, among the heavens there is a heaven in which there is no place except that an angel is in it prostrating, or his two feet standing; then he recited: ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks, and indeed We are those who glorify [Him]﴾.

* Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya related to us, saying: al-Jurayri informed us, from Abu Nadra, who said: When the prayer was called, Umar would turn his face toward the people and say: "O people, straighten [your rows], for indeed Allah only wants you to have the guidance of the angels ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks, and indeed We are those who glorify [Him]﴾. Straighten up. Step forward, you; step back, you, O so-and-so." When they had straightened, he would advance and say the takbir.

* Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, saying: Abu Usama related to me, saying: al-Jurayri, Sa'id ibn Iyas Abu Mas'ud, related to me, saying: Abu Nadra related to me, saying: When the prayer was called, Umar would face the people and say: "Straighten your rows and be even, for Allah only wants you to have the guidance of the angels," saying: ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks, and indeed We are those who glorify [Him]﴾; then he mentioned something similar.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks﴾, he said: It means the angels. ﴿And indeed We are those who glorify [Him]﴾, he said: The angels are in ranks, glorifying Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks﴾, he said: The angels.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman related to us, saying: Abu Hilal related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks﴾, he said: The angels.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks﴾, he said: Rows in the heaven. ﴿And indeed We are those who glorify [Him]﴾: that is, those who pray. This is the saying of the angels, praising their own standing in worship.

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks﴾, he said: For prayer.

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: al-Suddi mentioned, from Abdullah, who said: There is no place the size of a span in the heaven except that upon it is the forehead or the two feet of an angel, prostrating, standing, or bowing; then he recited this verse: ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks, and indeed We are those who glorify [Him]﴾.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks﴾, he said: The angels; all of this is for them.

Interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they disbelieved in it, but they will soon know﴾ (170) ﴿And We had already preceded in Our word to Our servants, the messengers﴾ (171) ﴿that they would indeed be given victory﴾ (172) ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers, they will be the victorious﴾ (173).

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿If only we had with us a reminder from the earlier peoples, we would surely have been sincere servants of God﴾ [37:168–169]. * *

And His saying: ﴿And We had already preceded in Our word to Our servants, the messengers, that they would indeed be given victory﴾

God, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And We had already preceded in Our word to Our messengers that they would indeed be given victory." That is: this decree and judgment had already passed from Us in the Mother of the Book, namely that they would have victory and dominance through proofs.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We had already preceded in Our word to Our servants, the messengers﴾ up to ﴿they will be the victorious﴾, he said: This was preceded by God for them, that He would give them victory.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿And We had already preceded in Our word to Our servants, the messengers, that they would indeed be given victory﴾, he said: "through proofs."

Some of the Arabic grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyyah) interpreted it as: "And Our word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers, concerning happiness (bi-l-sa'adah)." It is mentioned that in the reading of 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) it is: "And Our word had already preceded upon Our servants, the messengers" (la-qad sabaqat kalimatuna 'ala 'ibadina al-mursalin), where "ʿalā" is put in place of "lām," so the meaning is: "It became binding upon them and for them," as it is said: "ʿalā mulk Sulayman" and "fī mulk Sulayman," since the meaning of both is one.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers, they will be the victorious﴾

He says: "And indeed, Our party and the people of Our allegiance, they will be the victorious"; that is, for them is triumph and success over the people of disbelief in Us and opposition to Us.

He said: they will see on the Day of Resurrection what they squandered of God's command, and their disbelief in God, His Messenger and His Book. He said: "watch them" and "they will see" are one and the same.

* *

He says: So with the descent of Our punishment upon them, they seek to hasten you, O Muhammad, and that is their saying to the Prophet: ﴿When will this promise be, if you are truthful?﴾

* *

The "sahah" (courtyard) is the open space in front of a man's house. ﴿Evil is the morning of those who were warned﴾ means: evil is the morning of the people whom Our messenger warned, when that punishment descended upon them, and they did not believe in it.

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said regarding this.
